classes.name: stzAgentHost
classes.brief: Supervises agents as cancellable, traced, quarantinable and decommissionable jobs ticked on a timer or on events.
classes.description: A host owns a reactor, or shares one. It ticks each supervised agent through its Cycle, on its own timer or once per event of a bus channel, and records a trace. Cancel is a pause anyone can undo; Quarantine is a containment act that only an effectful actor can lift with Release; Retire is permanent and earned, refused until the declared decommission obligations are fulfilled. SetActionBudget caps the acts an agent may take in a window and quarantines a runaway. UseEngineLoop hands the scheduling decision to the engine, which refuses an agent that states neither what it covers nor how reversible it is. UseAgentsFrom mounts agents written as files. The host keeps a copy of each agent: configure it fully before Supervise and reach it afterwards through AgentQ.

methods.name: StartOn
methods.brief: Bind a CHOSEN interface, so a backend can be reached from another MACHINE: StartOn("127.0.0.1", p)  loopback -- this process and its children only StartOn("0.0.0.0",   p)  every interface -- reachable across the network StartOn("10.0.0.7",  p)  one specific NIC
methods.detail: LEAVING THE LOOPBACK REQUIRES A KEY. On 127.0.0.1 the callers are this machine; on a real interface they are whoever can route to the port, and an unauthenticated MBaaS floor would take a POST from any of them. So a non-loopback bind without SetSigningKey() is REFUSED here rather than quietly exposed -- governed by construction, not by a later audit finding.

classes.name: stzAppServer
classes.brief: Hosts routes, a REST floor over a database, raw device streams and supervised agents on one resident event loop, served on a localhost-first HTTP listener.
classes.description: The server is a persistent host rather than a per-request library: Start binds a listener on a reactor (an engine thread), and the serve loop (ServeOne, RunFor or Run) drains framed requests, runs the matching handler and writes the answer back; no callback ever crosses into the Ring VM. One host serves four shapes. WEB: Get_, Post, Put_ and Delete add routes whose handlers receive a request and a response. MBaaS: Expose and ExposeWithKey turn a stzDatabase table into list, count and read, create, update, delete routes. IoT: ListenRaw opens a raw TCP listener whose handler answers with RawWrite. AGENTS: HostAgents attaches an agent host that shares the loop and ticks between serve slices, with a read-only view at GET /agents. /health is always answered and /metrics appears once Observe attaches a perf monitor. Bind to 127.0.0.1 unless the server must be reached from outside, and then call RequireSignedRequests; MountAuth and MountOidcProvider serve a login router and an identity provider from the same listener. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: Use and Static store their arguments but never act, and Stop leaves Port and Uptime unreset.
classes.example:
o1.Get_("/greet", func oReq, oResp { oResp.Text("hello") })
o1.Start(0, "127.0.0.1")
? o1.IsRunning()
#--> 1
o1.Stop()

classes.name: stzAuth
classes.brief: Authenticates the users of an app: keeps salted password hashes, opens and ends sessions, and resolves a login into roles and an actor.
classes.description: It holds a credential store (user name to a salted Argon2id hash, never the plaintext) and issues opaque 64-character session tokens. Around the password it offers a second factor (TOTP with recovery codes), passwordless doors (magic link, emailed code, passkey), external sign-in (OpenID Connect, SAML), a brute-force lockout, an administrative lock, password reset by mail, and roles that turn a live session into the stzSystemActor that governance reasons about. The store is in memory unless SetStore is given a database store. Every flow has an At form that takes the moment as epoch seconds, which makes expiry and lockout testable; the plain forms read the clock. Failures answer an empty text, 0 or [ ] instead of raising, except for a missing mail port, relying party, provider or client, which raise.

classes.name: stzBarPlot
classes.brief: Draws a list of numbers, or labelled numbers, as vertical bars: as text for a terminal, as SVG, or as a PNG picture.
classes.description: One plot object answers three ways. ToString (and Show) draws block characters, axes and labels in text; ToSVG needs no graphics device; ToPNG draws on the GPU. The setters (height, bar width and spacing, axes, labels, values, percentages, average line, characters) shape the text picture only: the SVG and PNG carry the values, the labels, AddValues and AddAverage and nothing else, and print no text unless a :Font option is given. Bars are scaled so the largest value fills the height. Setters answer nothing, so they cannot be chained. stzHBarPlot (sideways bars) and stzMBarPlot (grouped bars) inherit from it. Several settings store a value no picture reads today (SetWidth, SetMaxWidth and the width of SetSize), SetMaxLabelWidth does not truncate, and SetLabelChar renames labels taken from the keys; see their warnings. Gallery: doc/gallery/stzBarPlot/basic.png (average line), values.png (values above twelve bars) and nofont.png (no font: bars and gridlines only), each with its .ring script, seen right by stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG), 2026-10-05, not a person; terminal.txt is the text picture, read as text and judged right.

classes.name: stzCalendar
classes.brief: Holds a period of days (a year, a quarter, a month or a date range) with working days, holidays, breaks and business hours, and counts available days and hours.
classes.description: Build it from a year (2026), a month ([ 2026, 3 ] or the text 2026-03), a quarter (2026-Q2 or [ 2026, "Q2" ]), a date range ([ [ "Start", "2026-03-10" ], [ "End", "2026-03-20" ] ]) or a single date. Set the working weekdays with SetWorkingDays (Monday to Friday is the default, set the first time IsWorkingDay runs), the hours with SetBusinessHours (09:00:00 to 17:00:00 by default), and add holidays with AddHoliday and daily breaks with AddBreak. Then ask for working days, available days and available hours of the whole period or of one day (AvailableHoursOnN), check that a task fits (CanFit, FirstAvailableSlot), attach a stzTimeLine to look for conflicts, compare two calendars, and export the facts with ToHash, ToJSON and ToCSV or draw them with Show, ShowHeatMap and ShowTable. Hours are whole hours, rounded down day by day. Month and year navigation moves the calendar itself. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: only the FIRST day of a period is checked against the holidays when days are counted (the next days are produced as dd/MM/yyyy text, while holidays are compared as text with the date as added); about twenty methods are stubs that raise Not yet implemented!, or call a method that does not exist (the Between families of breaks, working days and available days, GoToNext, ConflictsWithSpan, ContainsBreaksBetween); AvailableHoursBetweenN overwrites the whole-calendar cache; FirstAvailableSlot ends its slot from midnight; ContainsBusinessHours is always FALSE; going to the next month from December raises; a year or quarter calendar cannot be drawn.

sections.title: navigating the calendar back and forth

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the calendar of a year, a month, a quarter, a date range or a single date, with Monday to Friday and 09:00 to 17:00 as defaults.

parameters.name: p
parameters.role: what the calendar covers: a year above 1900 such as 2026, a text such as 2026-03, 2026-Q2 or 2026-03-15, a list such as [ 2026, 3 ] or [ 2026, "Q3" ], or named pairs such as [ [ "Start", "2026-03-10" ], [ "End", "2026-03-20" ] ] or [ :Year = 2026, :Month = 3 ]

notes: named pairs accept Start or From, End or To, Year, Month, Quarter; the working days stay empty until SetWorkingDays or the first IsWorkingDay, which sets Monday to Friday; the locale key is never read
warnings: a year of 1900 or less, a number with decimals, [ ] and [ 2026, 13 ] raise; 2026-q4 with a lowercase q raises R41 (only Q3 as the second list item is case- free); [ 2026, "Spring" ] silently gives the whole year; a plain list of two dates [ "2026-03-10", "2026-03-20" ] and a list holding only a Start pair leave the calendar empty; any other text, such as gregorian, becomes a one-day range whose dates cannot be read

classes.name: stzCanvas
classes.brief: Holds a 2D picture described once, as shapes and text, and gives it back as vector SVG or as pixels drawn on the graphics device.
classes.description: The Add methods remember the shape instead of posting it, so Fill, Stroke, Color and SetFont can still reach the last shape added; the shape is posted when the next one arrives or an output is asked for. Fill and Stroke called before any shape set the default for every shape added after. The plain form of a method acts and answers nothing, and its Q twin answers the canvas so calls can be chained; only the pick, identity and region setters answer the canvas without the Q. Text needs a font from SetFont. ToSVG needs no device and is the floor of the tier ladder; ToPNG and ToPixels go through the GPU and answer an empty string when none is available. Coordinates are pixels from the top-left corner, sizes run from 1 to 16384, and the SVG output draws circles, rounded rectangles, ellipses and strokes as polygons and polylines.

methods.brief: Counting (engine-backed, Ring-list-shaped).
methods.detail: Returns a Ring list of N values produced by cycling through (@nStartAt, @nStep) under the wrap-around modes :WhenYouReach and :AfterYouSkip. The cycle itself is built by the Zig engine in O(N) (see ring_bridge_intseq.zig), then marshalled into a Ring list via the engine bridge. Callers see a plain list and never need to know an engine handle existed. The previous Ring-only loop (aResult + n inside a class method) was O(N^2) on Ring 1.26 because the attribute table is re-walked per append; the engine path is the only correct implementation now and is named with the natural Softanza verbs (Counting / Count / CountTo / CountingTo). The engine-flavoured *Seq aliases that existed during the bring-up phase have been retired -- callers that genuinely want the raw stzIntSeq handle (e.g. for streaming Sum/Min/Max over a billion-element cycle without materialising) can call the dedicated _Handle accessor below.

classes.name: stzDataSet
classes.brief: Holds a list of numbers or categories and answers descriptive, distribution, relation and quality questions about it, with rules that turn the figures into written insights.
classes.description: The data type is detected when the set is built (numeric, categorical, mixed or empty) and missing markers such as NA are dropped. Numeric statistics answer 0 for data that is not numeric, and the count-based ones need two to four values. The methods fall in groups: the descriptive ones (Mean, Median, Mode, spread, quartiles, Percentile), frequency and diversity for categories, shape and outliers (Skew, Kurtosis, Outliers, ZScores, TrendAnalysis), relation to a second data set given as an argument (CorrelationWith, RegressionCoefficients, ChiSquareWith, MutualInformation), scaling (Normalize, Standardize, RobustScale), and the insight layer: domain rules (AddInsightRule, InsightsOfDomain), plans (MakePlan, ExecutePlan) and Summary. The tables of rules and plan templates are global, shared by every data set of the process, and ExecutePlan and AdaptiveAnalysis print as they work. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: Percentile makes the engine panic for a percent below 0 or far above 100, WMean overflows the stack, NonParametricCorrelation and PlanSummary raise errors, and MutualInformation misreads values that contain an underscore.

classes.name: stzDate
classes.brief: Holds one calendar date (year, month, day) with no time of day, moves it by days, months or years, compares it and writes it in several formats.
classes.description: A stzDate is three numbers. Build it from a text (2026-03-15, 15/03/2026, 15.03.2026, 15032026, today, in 3 days), from a list [ 2026, 3, 15 ], from a hash with :Year, :Month and :Day, or from an empty text for today. A text with a 4-digit first part is read year-first, any other text day- first, so 03/15/2026 raises. The Add and Subtract methods move the object itself and return nothing (the Q forms answer the object so calls chain); the Next, Previous, Start and End methods answer a text in dd/MM/yyyy and leave the object alone (their Q forms answer a copy). Measure with DaysTo, WeeksTo, MonthsTo and YearsTo, compare with IsBefore, IsAfter, IsEqualTo and IsBetween, and write it with ToString (dd/MM/yyyy), ToISO8601, ToAmerican, ToLong or ToStringXT with a format such as yyyy-MM-dd. Dates before 1970 work, because the engine counts civil days and not Unix seconds. Today follows StzFreezeClock, so a test can pin it. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: MonthsTo, YearsTo, IsSameWeek, IsSameMonth, IsSameYear and IsBetween raise for anything but a stzDate object; DaysTo and the Is comparisons overwrite a list or hash variable of the caller; PreviousWeekday answers a Saturday from a Sunday; Age counts year numbers only; a language given with a capital (French) falls back to English; a list or hash given to the constructor is not validated.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the date from a date text, a [ year, month, day ] list, a hash with :Year, :Month and :Day, or today when the text is empty.

parameters.name: pcDate
parameters.role: a date text such as 2026-03-15 or 15/03/2026, the words today, yesterday or tomorrow, a phrase such as in 3 days, a list [ 2026, 3, 15 ], or a hash [ :Year = 2026, :Month = 3, :Day = 15 ]

notes: text with 4 digits first is read year-first (yyyy-MM-dd, yyyy/M/d), otherwise day-first (dd/MM/yyyy, dd.MM.yyyy, ddMMyyyy); an empty text is today and follows StzFreezeClock; dates before 1970 are fine here, unlike stzDateTime
warnings: a text is checked (2026-02-30 raises Invalid date provided!) but a list or hash is not (13 as month is stored and IsValid answers FALSE); text with the month first such as 03/15/2026 is read day-first and raises; a number, or a list that is not 3 numbers, raises Can't create the stzDate object; a two- digit year (15-03-26) raises R41; a phrase with a unit other than day, week, month, year, decade or century leaves the date empty without an error

warnings: a text with an impossible day (2026-02-30) raises Invalid date provided! only AFTER the fields were overwritten, so the object keeps the invalid date; a phrase with an unknown unit changes nothing

classes.name: stzDateTime
classes.brief: Holds one date and time, to the millisecond, and adds to it, compares it, measures distances from it and writes it in many formats.
classes.description: A stzDateTime is made of seven numbers (year, month, day, hour, minute, second, millisecond) that read as one instant with no time zone: ToUTC and ToLocalTime change nothing. Build it from a text (2026-03-15 14:30:00, 15/03/2026 2:30 PM, an ISO text with a T), from a number of seconds since 1970, from a hash of parts, or from an empty text for the current clock. The Add and Subtract methods move the object itself and answer the new text; the Q forms answer the object so calls chain. Compare with IsBefore, IsAfter, IsEqualTo and IsBetween; measure with the DurationTo family (against another datetime) and the DurationSince family (against a named origin such as :UnixEpoch or :YearOne). The To... methods write it as text: ToIso for storage, ToStandard and ToAmerican for display, ToHuman and ToRelative in words. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: instants before 1970 and every origin but :UnixEpoch give an invalid date, the Verbose family and ToLongDate print the letter d instead of the day, ParseNaturalEpoch counts plural units twice, and three Milliseconds methods raise.

methods.name: ToTextDate
methods.brief: Returns the weekday, month and day with a 24-hour time and the year, in ddd MMM d HH:mm:ss yyyy order.
methods.returns: a string such as Sun Mar d 14:30:00 2026 today
notes: the intended text is weekday, month, day, time and year
warnings: the day of the month comes out as the letter d (Sun Mar d 14:30:00 2026) because the single d of the pattern is never replaced

methods.name: ToSimple
methods.brief: Returns day/month/year with the hour on a 12-hour clock and an AM/PM marker, without seconds.
notes: the hour is not zero padded; the marker texts come from the default locale

methods.name: ToSimple24h
methods.brief: Returns day/month/year with a 24-hour time, without seconds.

methods.name: ToLong
methods.brief: Returns the weekday, month name, day, year and a 12-hour time with seconds and an AM/PM marker.
methods.returns: a string such as Sunday, March 15, 2026 2:30:00 PM
notes: the day and month names are English; the hour is not zero padded

methods.name: ToLong24h
methods.brief: Returns the weekday, month name, year and a 24-hour time with seconds, with the day number printed as the letter d today.
methods.returns: a string such as Sunday, March d, 2026 14:30:00 today
notes: the intended text is Sunday, March 15, 2026 14:30:00
warnings: the day of the month comes out as the letter d because the single d of the pattern is never replaced; ToLong prints the day correctly

methods.name: ToLongDate
methods.brief: Returns the weekday, month name and year without a time, with the day number printed as the letter d today.
methods.returns: a string such as Sunday, March d, 2026 today
notes: the intended text is Sunday, March 15, 2026
warnings: the day of the month comes out as the letter d because the single d of the pattern is never replaced

methods.name: ToString12h
methods.brief: Returns yyyy-MM-dd with the time on a 12-hour clock, seconds and an AM/PM marker.
notes: the hour is not zero padded

methods.name: ToHuman
methods.brief: Returns a sentence such as Sunday, March 15th, 2026 at Half past 2 PM, with the time said in words.
notes: whole times read 12 o'clock, quarter hours read Quarter past or Quarter to, other times read like 9:05 AM

methods.name: ToRelative
methods.brief: Returns how far the datetime is from the system clock in words, such as 5 minutes ago, in 3 hours or just now.
notes: under 60 seconds is just now; then minutes, hours, days, weeks, months of 30 days and years of 365 days, rounded to the nearest unit; depends on the clock when it is called

methods.name: Copy
methods.brief: Returns a new stzDateTime holding the same date and time, so the copy can change without touching this one.
notes: the object is not changed

methods.name: SetComponents
methods.brief: Sets year, month, day, hour, minute, second and optionally millisecond from a list, and answers the object itself.

parameters.name: aComponents
parameters.role: a list [ year, month, day, hour, minute, second ] with an optional seventh number for the milliseconds

methods.returns: the object itself, so calls can be chained
notes: the SetComponentsQ form gives the same result
warnings: does not check ranges, so a month of 13 is stored and IsValid then answers FALSE; a list shorter than 6 numbers is ignored

extensions.name: SetComponentsQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Components
methods.brief: Returns the parts as the list [ year, month, day, hour, minute, second, milliseconds ].

methods.name: IsValid
methods.brief: TRUE if the month is 1-12, the day exists in that month (leap years included) and the time fields are in range.
notes: checks hour 0-23, minute 0-59, second 0-59 and milliseconds 0-999

methods.name: IsAStzDateTime
methods.brief: TRUE if the object is a datetime object, which is always the case here; callers use it to tell classes apart.

methods.name: IsNaturalEpochString
methods.brief: TRUE if the text contains from epoch or since epoch, in any case.

parameters.name: cStr
parameters.role: the text to examine

notes: only the phrase is tested, not the amount before it

methods.name: ParseNaturalEpoch
methods.brief: Sets the object to 1970-01-01 plus a duration in words, but counts each plural unit more than once today (2 days gives 4).

parameters.name: _cNatural_
parameters.role: the duration in words ending with from epoch or since epoch, such as 3 days 2 hours from epoch

methods.returns: nothing; the object changes in place
notes: FromNaturalEpoch reads the same words correctly; the constructor uses this method for text with from epoch or since epoch
warnings: counts every plural unit twice or three times: the unit list holds days and day, minutes, minute and min, seconds, second and sec, and each one is found inside the plural word, so 5 minutes gives 15 minutes and 2 days gives 4 days; singular units such as 1 week are right

methods.name: SetFromEpochMonths
methods.brief: Sets the object to the first day of the month n calendar months after January 1970, at 00:00:00.

parameters.name: _nMonths_
parameters.role: the number of months since January 1970

methods.returns: nothing; the object changes in place
notes: the same as FromMonthsSinceEpoch with the Unix origin
warnings: a negative count leaves a month of 0 or less, an invalid date

methods.name: SetFromEpochYears
methods.brief: Sets the object to January 1 at 00:00:00 of the year 1970 plus n.

parameters.name: _nYears_
parameters.role: the number of years since 1970

methods.returns: nothing; the object changes in place

methods.name: SetFromEpochDuration
methods.brief: Sets the object to 1970-01-01 plus a hash of durations, milliseconds included, such as [ :days = 3, :milliseconds = 250 ].

parameters.name: aHash
parameters.role: a hash whose keys are years, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds or milliseconds

methods.returns: nothing; the object changes in place
notes: unlike FromEpochHash it reads the :milliseconds key
warnings: a negative total gives an invalid date

methods.name: IsCountingFromString
methods.brief: TRUE if the text contains counting from, starting from or since, in any case.

parameters.name: cStr
parameters.role: the text to examine

notes: since alone is enough, so any text with since in it answers TRUE

methods.name: ParseCountingFrom
methods.brief: Sets the object from a text such as 2 days counting from unix epoch (a duration, a phrase, an origin); does nothing without a phrase.

parameters.name: cStr
parameters.role: the text, a duration then counting from, starting from or since, then an origin name in words

methods.returns: nothing; the object changes in place
notes: the origin words are turned into an origin name by MapOriginName
warnings: an origin before 1970 (year one, atomic age...) leaves an invalid date today

methods.name: MapOriginName
methods.brief: Returns the origin name that matches words such as year one, atomic age or us independence; unknown words give unixepoch.

parameters.name: cName
parameters.role: the origin in words, any case

methods.returns: an origin name as lowercase text, such as yearone
notes: matching is by phrase: unix, year one or common era, islamic, space age, atomic age, us independence, french revolution, internet
warnings: modern computing is not recognised and answers unixepoch like any unknown text

methods.name: SetCountingFrom
methods.brief: Sets the object to an origin plus a number of seconds, or plus a hash of durations; an empty origin means 1970-01-01.

parameters.name: _nValue_
parameters.role: the seconds after the origin, or a hash such as [ :hours = 5 ]

parameters.name: _cOrigin_
parameters.role: the origin name as a symbol or lowercase text

methods.returns: nothing; the object changes in place
notes: seconds may carry a fraction, which becomes the milliseconds
warnings: every origin except :UnixEpoch lies before 1970 and leaves an invalid date today; mixed-case origin text counts as the Unix epoch

methods.name: GetOriginBase
methods.brief: Returns an origin's distance from 1970-01-01 in milliseconds, negative for earlier origins; 0 when the name is unknown.

parameters.name: _cOrigin_
parameters.role: the origin name as a symbol or lowercase text, such as :YearOne

notes: the nine origins are UnixEpoch, YearOne, IslamicHijra, USIndependence, FrenchRevolution, AtomicAge, SpaceAge, InternetAge and ModernComputing
warnings: an origin written as mixed-case text such as "YearOne" is not found and answers 0

methods.name: SetFromNaturalDuration
methods.brief: Sets the object to an origin plus a duration in words such as 1 day 1 hour; an empty origin means 1970-01-01.

parameters.name: _cDuration_
parameters.role: the duration in words, numbers each followed by years, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes or seconds

parameters.name: _cOrigin_
parameters.role: the origin name as a symbol or lowercase text

methods.returns: nothing; the object changes in place
notes: a year counts 365 days and a month 30.4 days
warnings: an origin before 1970 leaves an invalid date today; milliseconds are not read

methods.name: ParseNaturalDuration
methods.brief: Returns the milliseconds that a duration in words such as 10 minutes 5 seconds adds up to.

parameters.name: _cDuration_
parameters.role: the duration in words, numbers each followed by years, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes or seconds

notes: a year is 365 days and a month 30.4 days; the object is not changed
warnings: a word instead of a number (two days) raises R41; milliseconds are not read; only the first amount of each unit counts

methods.name: HashToMilliseconds
methods.brief: Returns the milliseconds that a hash of durations such as [ :days = 1, :hours = 1 ] adds up to.

parameters.name: aHash
parameters.role: a hash whose keys are years, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes or seconds

notes: a year is 365 days and a month 30.4 days; the object is not changed
warnings: a :milliseconds key is ignored today

methods.name: DurationTo
methods.section: duration calculations to a target datetime
methods.brief: Returns the distance from the datetime to a target in one unit, or a hash of all units when the unit is empty.

parameters.name: pTarget
parameters.role: the target datetime, as a stzDateTime or a date-time text

parameters.name: pcUnit
parameters.role: the unit as text such as days, or written :In = :Days

methods.returns: a number in the unit, or a hash with keys milliseconds, seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, years, decades and centuries
notes: negative when the target is earlier; days and weeks round down, hours and smaller units can carry a fraction, months and years compare calendar numbers
warnings: an unknown unit raises Unsupported unit, and so does in days with a space

methods.name: DurationInDaysTo

parameters.name: pcUnit
parameters.role: the target datetime, as a stzDateTime or a date-time text

methods.name: DaysTo

methods.name: WeeksTo
methods.section: duration calculations to a target datetime
methods.brief: Returns the whole weeks of 7 days from the datetime to a target datetime, rounded down.

parameters.name: pcUnit

methods.name: DurationInMonthsTo
methods.section: duration calculations to a target datetime
methods.brief: Returns how many calendar months apart the two datetimes are, by month number and ignoring the day.

parameters.name: pcUnit
parameters.role: the target datetime, as a stzDateTime or a date-time text

methods.returns: a whole number of calendar months
notes: 15 March to 1 April is 1 month, and 15 March to 14 April is also 1

methods.name: MonthsTo

methods.name: YearsTo

methods.name: TrainingSetQ
methods.brief: THE HELD SET IS LIVE THROUGH HERE.
methods.detail: Ring COPIES an object into an attribute, so the set handed to the constructor is a SNAPSHOT: growing the caller's own object afterwards would NOT reach this learner. Grow it through this accessor -- oLearner.TrainingSetQ().AddExample(...) -- which reaches the real held set (accessor + method call is live in Ring).

methods.name: Train
methods.brief: THE CASE FOLD HAPPENS ONCE HERE, not at every node (numeric phase 5).
methods.detail: ID3 compares categorical values case-insensitively, so "Sunny" and "sunny" are one value. The fold used to live inside _ValuesOf() and _Subset(), which means every row was re-folded once per (node, feature) pair -- and the value never changes. Profiled on 4000 examples x 8 features: _ValuesOf x20 over the set          0.338 s _Subset   x20 over the set          0.356 s StzLower  x20 alone                 0.297 s   <-- of that the same loops without it           0.022 s The fold was THIRTEEN TIMES the cost of the loop containing it, because StzLower builds two engine string objects and frees them -- five bridge crossings to lowercase one character. Folding the whole set once costs 0.129 s and the inner loops drop 4.2x. Third time this phase has found this shape: the CSV module's per-cell regex recompile, the linear solver's per-variable re-parse, and now this. The expensive line is rarely the one the plan names -- the plan said "trees -> engine", and the tree was never the problem.

classes.name: stzDeclaredLLMAgent
classes.brief: THE PROPOSER, AND WHAT IT MAY DO ON A TICK: read its input from memory, ask its stzLLMFunction for a STRUCTURED answer, and LEARN the result as facts.
classes.description: That is the whole of it. It writes into its own memory and nowhere else, it holds no effectful capability, and every field it learns had to satisfy the structure the file declared -- so a proposal that does not parse leaves no trace of itself in memory at all.

methods.name: SeedProposal
methods.brief: The offline door, and it is a METHOD rather than something a caller does through FunctionQ(): Ring copies an object on assignment, so `oF = oAg.FunctionQ()` then `oF.SeedAnswer(...)` seeds a copy the agent will never read.
methods.detail: Seeding from inside the class writes the agent's own function, which is the only version that ticks.

methods.name: FunctionQ
methods.brief: The live function, so a caller can seed it, fake it or read its budget BEFORE the agent is handed to a host.
methods.detail: After the handoff the host's copy is the one that ticks -- the same rule stzAgentHost already states for every supervised agent.

methods.name: Cycle
methods.brief: ONE TICK. Returns 1 when a proposal was made AND validated, 0 otherwise -- and 0 always says why rather than passing for quiet.

classes.name: stzDeclaredPIAgent

methods.name: UseServices
methods.brief: the EXTERNAL-DEPENDENCY surface (service-virtualization phase 7) --- Attach the solution's stzServiceRegistry, so the delivery plan can rehearse every external dependency -- its current binding and the production credential it will need -- BEFORE anything runs, and so Deploy(:Production) can REFUSE a surface that still resolves to a fake.
methods.detail: ONE CAVEAT, and it is Ring's, not this method's: an attribute store COPIES (probed -- bind a service on your own handle afterwards and this delivery will not see it). So either finish configuring the registry BEFORE attaching it, or make later changes THROUGH the accessor, which reaches the stored object: oDelivery.ServicesQ().BindLiveQ(:payments, oImpl, "stripe_key").

methods.name: ProductionCredentials
methods.brief: The credentials a production deploy will require -- names only, never values.

methods.name: ServiceFindingsForProduction
methods.brief: REHEARSE THE GATE.
methods.detail: The registry only reports sandbox-in-production once its phase IS production, so a pre-flight check asks the question in that frame and then puts the phase back -- you learn what shipping would say without declaring that you are shipping. (The plane's own habit: rehearse, then commit.)

methods.name: AsRuleGraph
methods.brief: Project parts AND services into one graph, so a rule can ask the question neither side can answer alone: does a part that is BOUND TO A SITE (i.e. destined for production) depend on a service that is still a fake? See stzServiceRuleSet.

methods.name: InferNeedsIn
methods.brief: a first inference: scan the app source for capability markers -> keys.
methods.detail: Upgradeable to the stzCodeGraph call-edge analysis (lexical starting point).

methods.name: DeployTo
methods.brief: WHERE each part deploys in production: bind a target site to the part it hosts.
methods.detail: Site-first, part-second -- demystified: "deploy to <site>, the <part>". (Deploy(:Emulated) needs no sites -- it runs in the browser; production does.)

methods.name: SetActor
methods.brief: the executing actor -- governs whether Deploy(:Production) COMMITS or only rehearses (only an effectful actor may cross the governed bridge to reality).

methods.name: RequiresIn
methods.brief: what a part NEEDS from its host: memory / compute / storage (a stzResourceSpec).
methods.detail: Parallels NeedsIn (capabilities); here it is the physical footprint the target must provide -- the CI/IaC "resources.requests" idea.

methods.name: ShipBundle
methods.brief: ship an emulator's bundle DIRECTORY as a part's production artifact.
methods.detail: The bundle you built and debugged with Deploy(:Emulated) becomes what Deploy(:Production) ships -- the same tree, one directive. pBundle is a stzEmulator or a dir path.

methods.name: ShipSlice
methods.brief: ship only pcPart's SLICE of the bundle -- its app (index.html) + engine subset (stz_<part>.wasm) + the bridge (stz.js), not the whole mission-control.
methods.detail: A frontend deploys only what it needs to run.

methods.name: Plan
methods.brief: REHEARSE the placement & scope plan -- no bytes built. This is Build()'s thinking made visible (VSF rehearse->plan->commit).

methods.name: Deploy
methods.brief: Deploy() covers BOTH phases (Scope-Oriented: the deploy scope is the frame). :Emulated   -> the programming phase: generate the web-based mission-control emulator (via stzEmulator) where the whole solution runs and is debugged visually, part by part. :Production  -> the same parts cross the governed bridge to real target SITES.
methods.detail: Deploy(:Production) DRIVES a stzDeployment: it binds each part to its site (from DeployTo) and, IF the actor may commit (effectful), STORES + LAUNCHES it -- otherwise it returns the deployment as a rehearsal. Emulation rehearses in the browser; production commits.

classes.name: stzDeployKey
classes.brief: a deploy / SSH private key -- a credential the deployment backend hands to ssh/scp.
classes.description: A real backend writes the material to a private (chmod 600) file.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: A name, as text.

classes.name: stzDeployment
classes.brief: The act of placing a solution onto sites: bind each part to a target site, then store / launch / report -- GOVERNED.
classes.description: Reality-touching ops (Store/Launch) require an actor that Can("effectful"); an inference-only actor (an LLM) may rehearse the plan but commits nothing. This is the same governance crossing the rest of the System Foundation uses: expression is free, admission is governed.

methods.name: Log
methods.brief: the structured log of the deployment run -- queryable and renderable (oDep.Log().EntriesOfLevel(:error), oDep.Log().AsJson()).
methods.detail: Populated by Run().

methods.name: SetTarget

methods.name: RunAfter

Returns [ [name, op, part, siteName, [needs]], ... ], topologically ordered so every dependency precedes its dependants.

On any failure, the completed store/launch steps are ROLLED BACK in reverse -- the deployment is transactional. Returns [ committed(0/1), [ [stepName, outcome], ... ] ]. A deployment REFUSED upstream -- by the service gate in stzDelivery, say -- comes back untouched, and "nothing happened" is then assertable without reading the log.

classes.name: stzDetection
classes.brief: Declares one rule over a sequence of security events and judges a ledger against it, answering findings.
classes.description: Four shapes, each computable over a bounded ledger without a query language: a burst (n events of one kind inside a window), a sequence (one kind followed by another), any (one occurrence is the story) and unusual (the newest window judged against the same kind's own history, so the threshold is learned instead of written down). The unusual shape is honest: the newest window is judged against the windows before it, a cold start says nothing, and a flood that evicted its own baseline is reported as a warning. Findings come in the unified shape [ :rule, :subject, :where, :severity, :message ], so they join stzRuleReport. Corroborated holds an error back to a warning until two distinct event kinds agree. A detection with nothing watched raises when asked to judge.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a detection of that name, which watches nothing yet and reports its findings at error severity.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the detection's name, which becomes the rule of its findings

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the detection's name, the rule its findings carry.

methods.name: Kind
methods.brief: Returns the event kind the detection watches, trimmed and in lower case.
methods.returns: a text; empty until WhenKind sets it

methods.name: Shape
methods.brief: Returns which shape the detection has: burst, sequence, any or unusual.
methods.returns: a text; empty until a declaring call sets it

methods.name: Severity
methods.brief: Returns the severity its findings carry, which is error until AsWarning or AsInfo changes it.

methods.name: Meaning
methods.brief: Returns the sentence given by Explaining, which is added to every finding message.
methods.returns: a text; empty until Explaining sets it

methods.name: WhenKind
methods.brief: Sets the event kind to watch, and makes the shape any when no shape was chosen yet.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: the event kind to watch, trimmed and put in lower case

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: start every detection with it
warnings: the kind is not checked against the catalog, so a misspelled kind watches nothing and never fires

methods.name: Repeats
methods.brief: Makes the detection a burst: this many events of the watched kind inside the window fire it.

parameters.name: pnTimes
parameters.role: how many events make a burst

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: the BURST shape of stzDetection
warnings: without Within the window is 0 ms, so only events stamped with the same millisecond count together

methods.name: Within
methods.brief: Sets the window of a burst or a sequence, in milliseconds of event wall time.

parameters.name: pnMs
parameters.role: the window length, in milliseconds

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain

methods.name: PerActor
methods.brief: Counts events actor by actor instead of across all actors, for a burst or an unusual rate.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: credential stuffing is per account, not per installation

methods.name: ThenKind
methods.brief: Makes the detection a sequence: an event of this kind must follow one of the watched kind.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: the event kind that must follow, trimmed and put in lower case

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
warnings: the kind is not checked against the catalog, so a misspelled kind never follows and the detection never fires

methods.name: BySameActor
methods.brief: Requires both events of a sequence to come from the same actor.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: without it the whole ledger counts as one actor and a sequence gives one finding in all

methods.name: OnAnyOccurrence
methods.brief: Makes the detection fire on any single event of the watched kind, for kinds where one occurrence is already the story.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: one finding per matching event, at most 16

methods.name: Unusual
methods.brief: Makes the detection judge the newest window of the watched kind against the history of that same kind.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: the defaults are windows of 60000 ms, a baseline of 12 windows, 3 sigma and a floor of 3 (threat model R9)

methods.name: Buckets
methods.brief: Sets the width of one window of the unusual shape, in milliseconds.

parameters.name: pnMs
parameters.role: the window width, in milliseconds, at least 1

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: the baseline is this width times AgainstBaseline
warnings: a width below 1 raises an error, and a value that is not a number raises R41

methods.name: AgainstBaseline
methods.brief: Sets how many windows before the newest one form the baseline of the unusual shape.

parameters.name: pnBuckets
parameters.role: the number of baseline windows, at least 3

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: the newest window is judged against the windows before it, never against a baseline that includes itself
warnings: fewer than 3 raises an error; until the ledger reaches back over 3 baseline windows nothing is said, because a cold start is not an anomaly

methods.name: Sigma
methods.brief: Sets how many standard deviations above the baseline mean make a window unusual.

parameters.name: pnZ
parameters.role: the number of standard deviations

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: on a flat baseline, where the windows before all hold the same count, sigma is not used: any count above that mean and at or over the floor fires

methods.name: AtLeast
methods.brief: Sets the floor of the unusual shape: a window with fewer events than this never fires.

parameters.name: pnCount
parameters.role: the smallest number of events in the newest window that can fire

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AsOf
methods.brief: Judges the unusual shape at a given wall time instead of at the newest event, so a guard can be exact.

parameters.name: pnWallMs
parameters.role: the moment of judgement, in epoch milliseconds, 0 for the newest event

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Corroborated
methods.brief: Marks the detection so that an error finding drops to a warning unless the matched events span two distinct kinds.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: the corroboration law: one anomalous signal is a rumor, and the message says it is a single signal

methods.name: Explaining
methods.brief: Sets the one-sentence meaning that is added to every finding message and to the explanation.

parameters.name: pcMeaning
parameters.role: what the detection means, as text

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AsError
methods.brief: Sets the severity of the findings to error.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AsWarning
methods.brief: Sets the severity of the findings to warning.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AsInfo
methods.brief: Sets the severity of the findings to info.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain

methods.name: CheckAgainst
methods.brief: Judges a ledger and returns the findings in the unified rule shape, ready for stzRuleReport.

parameters.name: poLedger
parameters.role: the stzSecurityLedger to judge, read through its retained window

methods.returns: a list of [ :rule, :subject, :where, :severity, :message ] findings; [ ] when nothing matches
notes: the subject is security and where is the detection name, then a slash and the actor when there is one; at most 16 findings, so a storm reports and does not flood
warnings: raises an error when nothing is watched, so call WhenKind first

methods.name: LastEvidence
methods.brief: Returns the events that matched in the last check, so an incident can build its timeline from them.
methods.returns: a list of records; [ ] before any check or when nothing matched

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Returns the detection told as lines of text: its shape with its numbers, and its meaning when given.
notes: the first line reads Detection name [severity] followed by the shape

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the lines Explain returns, one per line.

classes.name: stzDiagram
classes.brief: Holds a flow diagram of typed, coloured nodes and labelled edges, and draws it as SVG or PNG with no graphviz, or exports it as DOT, Mermaid, JSON or the native .stzdiag text.
classes.description: A stzDiagram is a stzGraph with a look: a theme, a layout direction, edge routing, pen and arrow settings, 24 node shapes (AddCircle, AddBox, AddDiamond and so on, each a node with a type and a label equal to its id), clusters drawn as boxes behind their nodes, annotators, and visual rules over node and edge properties. The inherited stzGraph methods (AddNodeXTT, Connect, AddEdgeXT, NodeProperty, Edges) build the content. ToCanvas lays the diagram out and draws it natively; ToSVG, ToPNG and ToPages are the outputs, and after ToCanvas the Render methods report where everything was drawn and PickAt answers what lies under a pixel. On top of that picture sits a headless editor: OnPress, OnMove, OnRelease and OnCancel feed a pointer into a state machine, Edit runs commands that Undo and Redo take back, and Pin fixes a node in the layout. Ids are folded to lowercase. Known defects, each carried as a warning: PenWidth, NodesWith, propertiesLegend and SaveToStzDiagInFolder raise; Explain raises once a visual rule is registered; ComputeMetrics divides by zero for a diagram with no path of two nodes; ToSVG and ToPNG leave the last picture freed, so picking fails after them; ImportDiag into a diagram that holds the first node adds duplicates; the pen-width setters are named the wrong way round. Display and View need graphviz and a viewer and Step and RunIn need a window; none of the three was run.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzDiagram("flow"); o1.AddNodeXTT("start", "Order Received", [ :type = "start" ]); o1.AddNodeXT("validate", "Validate"); o1.AddNodeXTT("done", "Done", [ :type = "endpoint" ]); o1.AddEdgeXT("start", "validate", "next"); o1.AddEdge("validate", "done")

methods.brief: THE AUDIBILITY FLOOR
methods.detail: Colour's doctrine, transposed: a sound system that cannot fail an audibility check does not have one. The check is a MARGIN over the floor.

methods.name: MarginMetric
methods.brief: WHAT THE MARGIN IS MEASURED WITH, said out loud every time it is asked.
methods.detail: SS2 CLOSED THIS. The first version had to use unweighted RMS, because SN5's Loudness() integrates over 400 ms blocks behind a -70 LUFS gate and an 880 Hz tone at PEAK 0.50 reports -1000 -- silence -- at every duration below 400 ms. An earcon is shorter than one block, so the standard cannot see it. The margin now uses LoudnessOfSupport: the SAME K-weighting and the same -0.691 + 10log10(z) formula, over the sound's own length. It is not a standard LUFS figure and the metric name says so -- but it is the ear's own weighting rather than a flat average, which is the difference between a gate that models hearing and one that models arithmetic.

methods.name: RequiredMarginOf
methods.brief: The gate. A cue needs 10 LU of headroom over the room; an alert needs 20.

methods.name: WouldFireAt
methods.brief: THE PRIORITY CONTRACT
methods.detail: :OverDanger is REFUSED as a colour-style pair, and plan S.3 argues why: two sounds in one instant do not layer, they MASK, and masking is frequency-selective and asymmetric -- so there is no fixed answer to "what can be heard over danger". The answer is nothing. You drop, or you duck. Ducking needs a per-bus gain node and is SS3, not this session. THE DECISION IS A PURE FUNCTION of (state, meaning, now), so a guard can assert the contract on a machine with no audio device at all. Fire() calls exactly this, with the transport's clock.

methods.name: ToSoundOfSaying
methods.brief: THE COMPOSITE, as DATA: earcon, a gap, then the phrase, in ONE buffer.
methods.detail: One buffer rather than two players is what answers VC4's kill criterion. Two independent players sharing a speaker can mask each other (the phrase starting under the earcon's tail) and can clip where they overlap. Laid out in one buffer they are SEQUENTIAL by construction: nothing overlaps, so nothing masks, and the peak is the louder of the two rather than their sum. Needs no audio device, which is what lets a guard measure the composition on a machine that cannot play it.

methods.name: TickSpeech

methods.name: SpeakQueueToEnd
methods.brief: Drive the queue to the end. Occupies the thread, which is honest for a script; a program with a UI ticks instead.
methods.detail: ONE BUFFER, ONE DEVICE, and the reason it is allowed to work this way is a property of this method rather than a shortcut. Ticking speaks one phrase per transport, and a transport is a DEVICE: opened, played, closed, per phrase. Three announcements meant three device open/close cycles, each costing about half a second of silence before its phrase and risking the end of the one before -- a device is closed the moment its last frame is READ, which is not when it is heard. This method OCCUPIES THE THREAD. Nothing can call Say while it runs, so the queue it starts with is the queue it finishes with: there is nothing left to cancel, and rendering the whole of it into one buffer is not a loss of behaviour, only of churn. TickSpeech keeps the per-phrase transport precisely because a program that ticks CAN be interrupted, and there the ability to stop mid-sentence is the point.

methods.brief: Total events emitted on the channel SINCE IT WAS CREATED -- the signal an event-driven consumer polls to detect new work.
methods.detail: It rises and never falls WHILE THE CHANNEL LIVES, which is not the same as monotonic, and the difference bites. DestroyChannel and ClearAll below put a channel back to zero, so a consumer holding a previous count sees a SMALLER number and, if it only tests for "bigger than last time", decides there is no new work -- for good. classes.name: stzFolder
classes.brief: Holds a folder as a position you can walk, and lists, finds, searches, edits, creates, copies and deletes the files and folders under it.
classes.description: A stzFolder is built on a path, created when it is missing, and keeps a current position, a home to return to (GoHome) and a history (GoBack). Listings are of the position, in lowercase: Files and Folders give the direct children as /name and /name/, DeepFiles and DeepFolders walk the whole tree. Find, Search and Modify come in three reaches: this folder (FindFiles, SearchInFiles, ModifyInRoot), one named child folder, and the Deep forms below. Ring has one process folder, and relative paths that reach the disk directly (a few of the In and Deep methods, IsInside, IsFolderEmpty) are read from it and not from the position, so pass absolute paths to those. Many file methods finish by moving the position to the file's folder; that step calls GetDirectoryPath, which exists nowhere, so with batch mode off (the default) they end in error R14, after the work for the create, remove, copy and move methods and before it for the others. Call SetBatchMode(1) first. The delete methods are real: DeleteFolder, DeleteAll, Erase, DeepRemoveAll and DeepErase remove what they name, and GoUp can lift the position above the home, so point an object at a folder you can afford to lose. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: FindFolders and CountFolder never match a plain name, Find and DeepFind nest the folders list inside the files list, DeepContainsOneOf... answer for all the names, FilesIn and FoldersIn raise for any non-empty child, SearchInFolder reports the wrong file, the Deep modifiers and DeepDeleteFile and DeepDeleteFolder do nothing, and FileOverwrite, FileSafeOverwrite, FileErase, FileSafeErase and FileBackup raise errors.

methods.brief: TRUE if batch mode is on, so file and folder operations leave the current position alone.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE by default

methods.name: SetBatchMode
methods.brief: Turns batch mode on or off; on, the create, delete, read and write methods no longer try to move into the folder they touched.

parameters.name: b
parameters.role: 1 to turn batch mode on, 0 to turn it off

methods.returns: nothing; the object is changed in place
notes: Turn it on before using the file methods: with it off, most of them end by calling GetDirectoryPath, which exists nowhere, and raise error R14
warnings: Raises an error for any value but 1 or 0

methods.name: CurrentPath
methods.brief: Returns the current position as text with a trailing slash, so a relative name can be joined to it directly.
notes: WorkingDirectory and pwd are the same method

methods.name: GoTo
methods.brief: Moves the current position to a folder below it, writing the old position to the history; the folder is not checked to exist.

parameters.name: _cPath_
parameters.role: a name or a path strictly below the current position

notes: MoveTo and cd are the same method; GoTo('..') is accepted as text and leaves a path with .. in it
warnings: Raises an error for an empty text or for a path that is not strictly below the position, an absolute path included when it is the position itself or above

methods.name: GoUp
methods.brief: Moves the current position to its parent folder, writing the old one to the history; it may leave the home folder.
notes: Nothing stops it going above the folder the object was created with, and the delete methods then act on that parent; Up and cdUp are the same method
warnings: Raises an error at a drive or filesystem root

methods.name: GoHome
methods.brief: Moves the current position back to the folder the object was created with, writing the old one to the history.
notes: GoToHome, GoToRoot and GoRoot are the same method

methods.name: GoBack
methods.brief: Moves the current position back to the last one in the history and removes that entry.
notes: Back and Previous are the same method
warnings: Raises an error when the history is empty

methods.name: PathHistory
methods.brief: Returns the positions the object has left, oldest first.
notes: NavigationHistory is the same method; every GoTo, GoUp, GoHome adds one

methods.name: ClearHistory
methods.brief: Empties the history of positions.
methods.returns: nothing; the object is changed in place

methods.name: IsAtHome
methods.brief: TRUE if the current position is the folder the object was created with.
notes: IsAtRoot is the same method

methods.name: RelativePathFromHome
methods.brief: Returns "." at home; away from home it raises error R14 today instead of returning the path from home.
methods.returns: text, "." at home; error R14 anywhere else
warnings: Raises error R14 away from home because it calls GetRelativePath, which exists nowhere

methods.name: DistanceFromHome
methods.brief: Returns 0 at home; away from home it raises error R14 today instead of counting the folder levels from home.
methods.returns: a number, 0 at home; error R14 anywhere else
warnings: Raises error R14 away from home because it calls GetRelativePath, which exists nowhere

methods.name: NavigationInfo
methods.brief: Returns pairs describing the position: home, current, relativefromhome, distancefromhome and history; away from home it raises error R14.
methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs at home; error R14 anywhere else
warnings: Raises error R14 away from home because it calls GetRelativePath, which exists nowhere

methods.name: CreateFolder
methods.brief: Creates a folder below the current position, with every missing level, and moves into it unless batch mode is on.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: a folder name or path below the current position

methods.returns: 1 (TRUE); also 1 when the folder already exists
notes: FolderCreate and MakeFolder are the same method; a relative path is joined to the position the object is at, which is inside the previous folder after a first CreateFolder
warnings: Raises an error for an empty text or for a path outside the current position

extensions.name: CreateFolderQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: CreateFolders
methods.brief: Creates several folders below the current position, each with its missing levels, without moving.

parameters.name: paNames
parameters.role: a list of folder names or paths below the current position

notes: MakeFolders and CreateSubFolders are the same method
warnings: Raises an error when the argument is not a list

extensions.name: CreateFoldersQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: CreatePath
methods.brief: Creates a deep folder path below the current position, every missing level included, without moving.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: a path below the current position

methods.returns: 1 (TRUE); also 1 when the path already exists
notes: MkPath and CreateDeepPath are the same method
warnings: Raises an error for an empty text or for a path outside the current position

extensions.name: CreatePathQ

extensions.name: MkPathQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: CreateDeepPathQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: DeleteFolder
methods.brief: Deletes a folder with everything inside it; in the default mode it then raises error R14 instead of moving to the parent.

parameters.name: _cFolder_
parameters.role: the folder to delete, held directly here

methods.returns: the engine's answer, 1 on success, when batch mode is on
notes: FolderDelete, RemoveFolder and FolderRemove are the same method
warnings: Raises error R14 after the deletion unless batch mode is on, because it calls GetDirectoryPath, which exists nowhere; raises an error (Folder does not exist.) for a name not held here

methods.name: DeleteAll
methods.brief: Deletes every file and every subfolder held directly here, subfolders with their contents, keeps this folder, and goes home.
notes: DeleteAllFiles, DeepDeleteFiles, FilesDeepDelete and AllFilesDeepDelete are the same method; despite those names it removes subfolders too
warnings: Raises an error when something cannot be removed

methods.name: RemoveAll
methods.brief: Deletes every file and every subfolder held directly here, keeps this folder, and goes home.
notes: RemoveAllFiles, DeepRemoveFiles, FilesDeepRemove and AllFilesDeepRemove call DeleteAll
warnings: Raises an error when something cannot be removed

methods.name: DeepRemoveAll
methods.brief: Removes this folder itself with everything in it; the object then points to a folder that no longer exists.
notes: DeepRemove and RemoveTree are the same method

methods.name: Erase
methods.brief: Deletes the files held directly here and keeps the folders.
notes: RemoveFiles is the same method; the position does not change

methods.name: DeepErase
methods.brief: Deletes every file of the whole tree below and keeps all the folders.

methods.name: DeepDeleteFile
methods.brief: Raises an error today instead of deleting the files of that name anywhere below.

parameters.name: cFileName
parameters.role: the file name to delete

methods.returns: nothing; the error Can't navigate outside the folder! is raised
notes: FileDeepDelete, DeepRemoveFile and FileDeepRemove call it
warnings: Always raises Can't navigate outside the folder!, because it tests the bare name against the process folder, so nothing is deleted (checked with a present and an absent name)

methods.name: DeepDeleteFolder
methods.brief: Does nothing today and answers 1 instead of deleting the folders of that name anywhere below.

parameters.name: _cFolderName_
parameters.role: the folder name to delete

methods.returns: 1, whether or not a folder was found
notes: DeepRemoveFolder is the same method; FolderDeepDelete and FolderDeepRemove call the file version by mistake
warnings: Deletes nothing: the folders found are relative paths and the existence test on them fails, so the loop skips every one (checked on a deep and on a top folder)

parameters.name: _cFile_
parameters.role: a file name held directly here, or its absolute path

methods.returns: text; the empty text for a folder name
notes: ReadFile is the same method; FileReadQ gives the reader object
warnings: Raises error R14 unless batch mode is on, because it calls GetDirectoryPath, which exists nowhere; raises an error for a file that is not held directly here, a deeper one included

extensions.name: OverwriteFileQ

warnings: Raises error R11 (class stzfileeraser not found) and erases nothing, so use FileRemove

extensions.name: FileEraseQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: EraseFileQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: FileSafeErase
methods.brief: Raises error R11 today instead of erasing a file safely; the file stays.

warnings: Raises error R11 (class not found) and erases nothing, so use FileRemove

extensions.name: SafeEraseFileQ

methods.name: FileRemove

parameters.name: _cFile_
parameters.role: a file name held directly here

notes: FileDelete, RemoveFile and DeleteFile are the same method
warnings: Raises error R14 after deleting unless batch mode is on

methods.name: FileBackup

parameters.role: the text that should replace the content

notes: SafeOverwriteFile is the same method
warnings: Raises error R11 (class not found) and writes nothing

methods.name: FileModify

parameters.name: cNewContent
parameters.role: the text to put in its place

notes: ModifyFile is the same method
warnings: Raises error R14 before changing anything unless batch mode is on

methods.name: FileCopy
methods.brief: Copies a file held directly here to a new name, replacing a file that is already there, and answers 1.

parameters.name: _cSourceFile_
parameters.role: the file to copy

parameters.name: _cDestFile_
parameters.role: the name or path of the copy

methods.returns: 1 (TRUE); 0 when the destination folder is missing
notes: CopyFile is the same method; an existing destination is overwritten without warning
warnings: Raises error R14 after copying unless batch mode is on; raises an error when the source is not held here

methods.name: FileMove
methods.brief: Moves a file held directly here to a new name or into another folder and answers 1.

parameters.name: _cSourceFile_
parameters.role: the file to move

parameters.name: _cDestFile_
parameters.role: the new name or path

methods.returns: 1 (TRUE); 0 when the destination folder is missing
notes: MoveFile is the same method; a move into a subfolder worked, and a move into a missing folder answers 0 and moves nothing
warnings: Raises error R14 after moving unless batch mode is on; raises an error when the source is not held here

methods.name: FileSize
methods.brief: Returns the size of a file held directly here, in bytes.

parameters.name: _cFile_
parameters.role: a file name held directly here

notes: FileSizeInBytes is the same method; an empty file answers 0
warnings: Raises error R14 unless batch mode is on; raises an error for a file that is not held directly here

methods.name: FileInfo
methods.brief: Returns pairs describing a file held directly here, such as its size, suffix and last modification time.

parameters.name: _cFile_
parameters.role: a file name held directly here

methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs, the keys in lowercase: name (without suffix), size, suffix, path, exists, iswritable, isreadable and lastmodified
notes: A folder name gives exists 0 and size -1

methods.name: FindFiles
methods.brief: Returns the files held directly here that match a name, a pattern with * or a list of names, ignoring case.

parameters.name: pPattern
parameters.role: a file name, a pattern with * as a wildcard, or a list of file names

methods.returns: a list of "/name" entries; [ ] when none match
notes: FindFile and FindThisFile are the same method; a.txt finds /a.txt and *.txt finds every .txt file
warnings: Raises an error for an empty text or a number; a lone * finds nothing

methods.name: FindFolders

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: a pattern with * as a wildcard, such as sub*

methods.returns: a list of "/name/" entries; [ ] when none match
notes: FindFolder and FindThisFolder are the same method; raises an error for an empty text
warnings: A plain name such as sub1, or /sub1/, answers [ ] because it is compared with the listing form /sub1/ after losing its slashes; only a * pattern can match

methods.name: FindFilesByExtension
methods.brief: Returns the files held directly here that end with an extension, ignoring case.

parameters.name: _cExt_
parameters.role: a file extension, with or without the leading dot

notes: FilesByExtension is the same method
warnings: Raises an error for an empty text

methods.name: FindTheseFiles
methods.brief: Returns the files held directly here that match any of a list of names or patterns, each file once.

parameters.role: a list of file names or * patterns

warnings: Raises an error when the argument is not a list

methods.name: FindTheseFolders
methods.brief: Returns the folders held directly here that match any of a list of * patterns, each folder once; plain names match nothing.

parameters.name: acFoldersNames
parameters.role: a list of * patterns, such as sub*

warnings: Raises an error when the argument is not a list; a plain name answers nothing for the reason given at FindFolders

methods.name: Find

notes: Use FindFiles and FindFolders for flat answers
warnings: The two lists are joined with the list-append operator, so the folders arrive as one nested item (a.txt gives [ "/a.txt", [ ] ] and sub* gives [ [ "/sub1/", "/sub2/" ] ])

classes.name: stzFont
classes.brief: Holds a loaded TTF or OTF typeface and measures text with it: widths, glyph positions, caret rectangles, and which glyphs a fallback chain had to borrow.
classes.description: The font is bytes you loaded, shaped by the engine's own pipeline (bidirectional analysis, HarfBuzz, stb_truetype), so a width can be trusted for layout in any script, Arabic included. Sizes are in pixels. A text that one font cannot draw comes out as hollow boxes, one per character; AddFallback puts other fonts behind it and CoverageOf counts what was borrowed and what is still missing. The caret and hit-test queries (RectsOfRange, CaretRectAt, IndexAtPoint) count bytes, not characters. The object holds one number, the engine's id for the face, so copies of the object share the same loaded font; after Free every measurement answers 0 or an empty list (and DrawsEveryGlyphOf answers TRUE, which is misleading). A stzCanvas draws text with a font set by SetFont.

classes.name: stzGeoAtlas
classes.brief: Binds the names and codes a caller types to the shapes of a boundary file the caller loaded, and reports what did not bind instead of guessing.
classes.description: A business table has a column of place names and wants a map: the user types USA and a shape appears. This class does the tedious and safe half: folding case, accents and punctuation, knowing that Burma and Myanmar are one country (about 50 aliases, each a fact about language, not about a border), finding a numeric id in a file that writes names, and a 2 or 3 letter code through the library's country table. The shapes are the CALLER'S file, never vendored here: the boundary data carries a position on every disputed border, a vintage and a licence the library will not own (test/graphics/atlas/README.md). A near miss is reported by Unresolved and never guessed, because a map that silently colours Niger for Nigeria is worse than one with a hole. IndexOf tries, in order, the file's id as written, the file's own name folded, an alias in either direction, then a country code. ValuesFor answers one value per feature, in the file's order, with the empty text where nothing bound: exactly what stzGeoMap.SetValues takes, so a table becomes a choropleth in two calls. Pictures, each looked at by 'stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG)' on 2026-10-05: doc/gallery/stzGeoAtlas/table_to_map.png, a typed table drawn on the world with the unbound keys listed and the unmentioned countries hatched, RIGHT; how_a_key_resolves.png, the page of 21 keys and what each found, RIGHT; niger_regions_table.png, a table with a misspelt region, RIGHT (the misspelt region and the forgotten one are hatched and named). Index: doc/gallery/INDEX_geo.md.

classes.name: stzGeoEllipsoid
classes.brief: Holds one reference ellipsoid by name and measures on it: shortest and constant-bearing paths, destinations, meridian and parallel lengths, ECEF and ENU frames, areas.
classes.description: Fifteen ellipsoids are known (WGS84, GRS80, WGS72, GRS67, Airy1830, AiryModified, Bessel1841, Clarke1866, Clarke1880, International1924, Krassovsky1940, Everest1830, AustralianNational, SouthAmerican1969 and Sphere) and WGS84 is the default everywhere, because it is what a GPS reports. The engine speaks metres and degrees: a method ending Km answers kilometres, one ending M metres. Mind the axis order: the point methods take LATITUDE FIRST, then longitude (DistanceKm, Azimuth, DestinationKm, MidpointOf ...), while every flat list of places (AreaKm2, PathLengthKm and the Flat methods) and every stzGeoProjection method take LONGITUDE FIRST; swapping them raises nothing and measures another pair of places. Niamey to Paris is 3919.43 km on WGS84 and 3931.58 km if the arguments are swapped. A shortest path (geodesic) is not a constant-bearing path (rhumb line): New York to London is 5585.2 km by the first and 5809.8 km by the second. Pictures, each looked at by 'stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG)' on 2026-10-05: doc/gallery/stzGeoEllipsoid/geodesic_vs_rhumb.png, a geodesic and a rhumb line on a Mercator, RIGHT (the rhumb line is straight, the geodesic bows toward the pole); doc/gallery/stzGeoEllipsoid/rings_and_areas.png, rings made with DestinationKm on an azimuthal equidistant map, RIGHT (they are true circles); ellipsoids_compared.png, six ellipsoids as the gap from WGS84 in metres and km2, RIGHT (the Sphere is 10.8 km long on Niamey to Paris). Index: doc/gallery/INDEX_geo.md.

classes.name: stzGeoFeatures
classes.brief: Holds the polygons, lines and points of a boundary file whole, every part and every hole, read from GeoJSON or TopoJSON, and answers what lies where.
classes.description: Build one with StzGeoFeaturesFromJson, StzGeoFeaturesFromTopoJson or StzGeoFeaturesFromJsonWhere, which also compute the boxes that make point-in-region tests fast. Each feature is a kind, an id, a hash list of properties and its parts; a polygon part is a list of rings, the first the outer edge and every one after it a hole. Every ring is closed, whichever format it came from. Coordinates are longitude then latitude, degrees, as both formats require, and every place-taking method here is LONGITUDE FIRST (Contains, IndexAt, Within). Nothing is simplified or reprojected, and this library vendors no boundary data: the atlas files are the caller's (test/graphics/atlas/README.md). Areas are measured on WGS84. One trap in the windows: a feature that crosses the antimeridian (Fiji, Russia, Antarctica) has a bounding box 360 degrees wide whose middle falls anywhere, so Within and IndicesWithin take Fiji for an Africa window. Pictures, each looked at by 'stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG)' on 2026-10-05: doc/gallery/stzGeoFeatures/parts_holes_lookup.png, parts, holes, an IndexAt raster of Niger and South Africa's hole, RIGHT; doc/gallery/stzGeoFeatures/window_and_areas.png, the areas panel RIGHT and the Within panel WRONG (Fiji is taken, see FINDINGS_geo.md); lines_points_kinds.png, a river, wells and a lake with a hole read from GeoJSON, RIGHT. Index: doc/gallery/INDEX_geo.md.

classes.name: stzGeoField
classes.brief: Holds a quantity that has a value everywhere, a grid of numbers over longitude and latitude, and draws it as a classed raster, as contours and with its legend.
classes.description: The grid is [ lon0, lat0, dlon, dlat, nx, ny ] with row 0 the SOUTH row, and an unknown node is the empty text, never a number: the commonest way an elevation map acquires a trench eleven kilometres deep is a NODATA of -9999 read as a depth. A field comes from StzGeoDensityField (the kernel density of a stzGeoPoints, in places per km2, edge-corrected and clipped to the window), from StzGeoFieldFromAsciiGrid (an ESRI ASCII grid, whose first text row is the north row and whose xllcorner is turned into a node centre) or from stzGeoSamples (inverse distance weighting and kriging). Classes must be set before DrawOn, which raises otherwise. The raster is resampled through the projection pixel by pixel, so a conic does not turn cells into wrong quadrilaterals. A field in per km2 refuses a projection that does not preserve area (FindingsOn). Set classes, ramp and unit on the field BEFORE putting it in a list: Ring copies an object it stores, so a change made through the list does not reach the original. Pictures, each looked at by 'stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG)' on 2026-10-05: doc/gallery/stzGeoField/rain_kriging.png, IDW, kriging and kriging variance of invented gauges, RIGHT (the variance is low at each gauge and high in the gaps); density_and_contours.png, a kernel density as raster and contours, RIGHT; ascii_grid_terrain.png, an ASCII grid read three ways, WRONG in one detail (a scatter of white pixels in the lowest class, see FINDINGS_geo.md). Index: doc/gallery/INDEX_geo.md.

classes.brief: Holds a map made of layers: a projection and a set of features, with values, classes, groups, labels, insets, legends, scale bar, sun and flows drawn on a canvas.
classes.description: Build it with StzGeoMap(oProjection, oFeatures) after fitting the projection to the features. The data layer takes one value per feature (SetValues, from stzGeoAtlas.ValuesFor, CountPointsIn or ValuesFromArea) or named groups (SetGroups), the classes are the author's (SetClasses, SetRamp, SetOpenTop) and a region with no value is hatched, never coloured as zero. SetPaper tells the map its sheet and should be the first call: labels are kept on it and the scale bar and the stream- density raster are measured over it. DrawSheetOn is the statistical map: dark hairline borders, the no-data hatch and the selection outlined; DrawLabelsOn writes a name inside its region or numbers it with a key; AddInset magnifies a place too small to label. A map judges itself (Findings, IsSound): a choropleth, a membership map or hexagon bins on a projection that is not equal-area is an error, as is a number with no key. Known gaps: with values set and no classes, ClassOf, ColourOf and the Draw methods that colour raise error R2; an inset does not copy SetOpenTop; DensityPointsIn is per 10000 km2. Pictures, each looked at by 'stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG)' on 2026-10-05: doc/gallery/stzGeoMap/niger_density.png, a density choropleth with inset, legend, scale bar and north arrow, RIGHT except the Niamey inset, which is grey instead of red (WRONG, see FINDINGS_geo.md); world_area.png, country areas on Equal Earth with a hatched no-data region, RIGHT; africa_blocs.png, a membership map, RIGHT; daynight_world.png, the night side and twilight on 2026-10-05, RIGHT; hexbin_flows.png, hexagon bins, area-true circles and great-circle routes, RIGHT; wind_streams.png and wind_arrows.png, an invented wind field, RIGHT as far as a picture can say. Index: doc/gallery/INDEX_geo.md.

methods.name: Bind
methods.brief: Binds the map to a projection and to the features it draws; raises an error unless both are objects.

parameters.name: poProjection
parameters.role: the stzGeoProjection that places everything

parameters.name: poFeatures
parameters.role: the stzGeoFeatures to draw

notes: StzGeoMap(oProjection, oFeatures) builds and binds in one call. Fit the projection to the features first

methods.name: Projection
methods.brief: Returns the projection the map draws with.

methods.name: Features
methods.brief: Returns the features the map draws.

methods.name: SetValues
methods.brief: Sets the value that colours each feature, one per feature in the features' own order, "" where there is none.

parameters.name: paValues
parameters.role: one number per feature, or "" for no data

notes: A region with no value is drawn as no data, never as zero. Set the classes before drawing: with values and no classes the Draw methods that colour raise error R2

extensions.name: SetValuesQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ValuesFromArea
methods.brief: Returns every feature's own area in square kilometres, a value that needs no other file.
methods.returns: a list of numbers, one per feature
notes: Measured on WGS84, like AreasKm2; an older comment in the source says sphere

methods.name: ValueOf
methods.brief: Returns the value of feature pnI.

parameters.name: pnI
parameters.role: the position of the feature, from 1

methods.returns: the stored value, or "" when pnI is outside the list of values

methods.name: SetClasses
methods.brief: Sets the class edges that colour the regions, and gives a Blues ramp of the right size when the number of classes changed.

parameters.name: paEdges
parameters.role: a rising list of at least two edges

notes: Raises an error for fewer than two edges or edges that do not rise. The edges are the author's: there are no automatic breaks

extensions.name: SetClassesQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SetRamp
methods.brief: Sets the class colours from a named ramp, in as many steps as there are classes.

parameters.name: pName
parameters.role: the ramp's name: :Blues, :YlOrRd, :YlGnBu, :Greens, :Oranges, :Purples, :Reds, :BuPu, :Earth, :Viridis, :Magma, :Cividis or :Flow

notes: Raises an error before the classes are set
warnings: Defect: the error for an unknown name lists nine ramps although thirteen exist (Viridis, Magma, Cividis and Flow are missing from the message).

extensions.name: SetRampQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SetPalette

parameters.name: pStroke

methods.name: CentroidOf

parameters.name: pnI
parameters.role: the position of the feature, from 1

methods.returns: a list [ lon, lat ]; [ ] for a position out of range
notes: A mean of vertices, not the area centroid: it follows the sampling, so on a ragged coast it slides toward the coast

methods.name: DrawHexBinsOn

parameters.name: paBins
parameters.role: the bins as HexBin answers them

parameters.name: pnRadius

parameters.name: paEdges

parameters.name: paPalette
parameters.role: one colour per class

methods.returns: nothing; the hexagons are added to the canvas

methods.name: HexBinMax

methods.name: DrawFlowsOn

parameters.name: poCanvas
