methods.detail: This is the whole of the in-scene input mapping (§6's tier): uv in, panel pixels out. v is flipped because a texture's origin is bottom-left and a panel's is top-left -- the one place that difference is stated, so no caller has to remember it.

methods.name: SetTextOf
methods.brief: the update path (G5)
methods.detail: BEFORE THESE, THIS CLASS COULD ONLY LOAD. Everything after LoadMarkup was a QUERY -- boxes, hit tests, focus, events -- so the only way to change what a screen said was to build the whole document again. `stzScenePanel.Shows` and the showcase's reload both do exactly that, and both say in their comments that they are the shape G5 replaces. This is that replacement. RmlUi re-lays-out what depends on the change and leaves every other string's shaped geometry alone -- which is not an optimisation we perform but one it already performs, once it is TOLD about the change instead of handed a new document. The difference is measurable, and the guard measures it: after a rebuild every string is generated again; after a set, only the ones that actually changed are. GenerateCalls() reports both. One element's words. The value is DATA -- it is escaped at the seam, so a model holding "<span>" cannot inject markup into a document the court already passed.

methods.name: TabRing
methods.brief: Walk the whole tab ring and answer the names in order. THE keyboard contract made checkable: a screen whose ring omits an action is a screen a keyboard cannot operate, and Rule 80 says that is a defect. Bounded, because a ring that never closes would otherwise hang.
methods.detail: A ring is a CYCLE, and this enters it wherever focus currently sits: RmlUi resumes tabbing from the last focused element even after a blur, so calling this with `cancel` focused answers the same cycle rotated. The SET and the ORDER are stable; the entry point is not. Call it before touching focus if the first stop matters -- as the guard does.

methods.name: Center
methods.brief: ── the choice you must make ──
methods.detail: THE NAME FORM CARRIES THE SEMANTICS, which is a Softanza law rather than a style: an ACTIVE verb -- Standardize(), Center() -- DOES the thing and returns nothing; the PASSIVE form -- Standardized(), Centered() -- returns the transformed DATA and leaves the object alone; and the Q twin does the thing and returns the object so calls chain. The first version of this class had Standardized() mutating the analysis and returning This, which got both halves wrong at once: a passive name for an active act, and a plain method returning an object where plain methods return data. CENTER each feature on its mean and leave the units alone -- covariance PCA. The features that vary most, in their own units, dominate.

methods.name: Standardize
methods.brief: CENTER and then divide each feature by its standard deviation -- correlation PCA. Every feature counts equally, whatever it was measured in.

extensions.name: StandardizeQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Centered
methods.brief: ── and the passive forms, which return the prepared DATA ── The data centered on the column means, original untouched.
methods.detail: This is what a covariance PCA actually decomposes, so it is worth being able to look at.

methods.name: Standardized
methods.brief: The data centered AND divided by the column standard deviations. What a correlation PCA decomposes.

methods.name: IsStandardized
methods.brief: TRUE if the object is standardized.

methods.name: UseSampleVariance
methods.brief: ── the variance convention, from the library's one authority ──

extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: UsePopulationVarianceQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: IsFitted
methods.brief: TRUE if the object is fitted.

methods.name: Components
methods.brief: The DIRECTIONS: row i, column j is how much feature i contributes to component j. A component is a weighted blend of your features, not one of them.
methods.detail: The sign is fixed by convention (the largest loading of each component is made positive) because a direction has no preferred sign -- v and -v are the same axis explaining the same variance -- and without a convention two runs can look like they disagree.

methods.name: Scores
methods.brief: The data in component coordinates: row i is sample i, column j its position along component j.
methods.detail: Centered by construction, so each column averages zero.

methods.name: ExplainedVariance
methods.brief: How much variance each component accounts for, in the units of the prepared data.
methods.detail: These SUM to TotalVariance() -- the decomposition redistributes the variance and cannot create or destroy any.

methods.name: ExplainedVarianceRatio
methods.brief: The same, as fractions of the total. This is the number people quote.

methods.name: NumberOfComponentsFor
methods.brief: How many components to keep to retain a given fraction of the variance -- the usual way the number of components is chosen.

methods.name: Mean
methods.brief: The centering that was applied, kept because projecting NEW data needs exactly the same one.
methods.detail: Data centered on its own mean lands in a different space.

methods.name: Inverse
methods.brief: Project rows the fit has not seen into the component space, using the FIT's centering and scaling. -- THE INVERSE, AND IT IS THE TRANSPOSE
methods.detail: This is where PCA differs in KIND from the rest of the embedding family, not merely in quality. The forward map is a ROTATION onto an orthonormal basis, so undoing it needs no second model, no training and no lookup: multiply by the same loadings the other way round, put the scale back, put the mean back. t-SNE and UMAP have no analytic inverse at all. They must fit a DECODER to (position, row) pairs, and what comes back is a plausible row rather than a recovered one. Here the arithmetic was already sitting in the fit. -- AND THE ERROR IS NOT MYSTERIOUS EITHER -- It is exactly the variance living in the components you dropped. Not approximately: the residual IS the projection onto the discarded eigenvectors, so the mean squared reconstruction error over the training rows EQUALS the sum of their eigenvalues -- the numbers ExplainedVariance() already reports. Keep every component and the reconstruction is the data back, to rounding. That identity is checked in the guard, and it is a far stronger statement than any reconstruction number the learned inverses can offer. It says the arithmetic is RIGHT, where they can only say the result looked plausible.

methods.name: Reconstructed
methods.brief: the training rows put through Transform() and back again -- what the analysis retained of the data it was given, which is the picture worth looking at when deciding how many components are enough

methods.name: Times
methods.brief: Convolution of the coefficient lists -- the definition of a product of polynomials. MULTIPLICATION IS A CONVOLUTION, which is why this has two paths.
methods.detail: The coefficients of a product are the convolution of the coefficients of the factors, so multiplying polynomials is exactly the operation an FFT does in O(N log N) instead of the double loop's O(n*m). stzFourier owns that convolution; nothing is reimplemented here. THE DOUBLE LOOP IS KEPT FOR SMALL DEGREES, and not out of caution: it is EXACT for integer coefficients, while the FFT route goes through irrational twiddle factors and comes back a few rounding errors away from a whole number. Below the crossover the direct method is both faster and more accurate, so preferring it is not a compromise. Above it, O(n log n) wins by enough that the rounding is worth paying.

methods.name: Call_
methods.brief: THE SYNCHRONOUS CALL. It has to actually call.
methods.detail: This built the task, handed it to AddTask, and returned it unexecuted. Its async sibling below calls Execute() on the local task; this one relied on the engine running it later, and the engine never saw it: @oEngine is an attribute, so AddTask appends to a COPY of the reactive system. Measured -- the real engine's task list stayed at zero, and after Start() the wrapped function had run zero times. Call_ did nothing whatsoever. AddTask is kept because CallAsync does the same and both are equally copy-bound; that is the engine-identity problem, not this method's, and papering over it here would hide it. Execute() on the LOCAL task is what makes the result real, which is exactly how CallAsync has always worked.

methods.name: SetReactor
methods.brief: The reactor is what makes the request path ASYNC -- _CanAsync answers FALSE without one and every verb falls back to the blocking task. NULL is therefore a legitimate value: it means "no reactor, go blocking".
methods.detail: Anything that is neither is refused rather than stored, because a bad reactor does not fail here; it fails later inside _SubmitAsync or DrainPending, a long way from the call that caused it.

methods.name: SetAutoConcludeDelay
methods.brief: Set the delay before auto-conclusion triggers.
methods.detail: It used to take anything at all: -500 and "not a number" both went straight through to a timer deadline. A refused value leaves the delay ALONE rather than resetting it -- a setter that answers a value it dislikes by destroying a good one is its own defect.

methods.name: ScheduleAutoConclude
methods.brief: Real-world timer implementation for auto-conclusion THE CALLBACK MUST BE HANDED THE OBJECT; it cannot reach for it.
methods.detail: This built a stzRingTimer whose callback was `func() { if @pendingDataCount = 0 ... }`. A Ring lambda has its own scope, and stzRingTimer stores the object it is given but then invokes `call @callback()` with NO arguments -- so the object was kept and never passed. The callback raised R24 "Using uninitialized variable: @pendingdatacount" on its first and only run, inside the timer runner, where nothing reported it. Auto-conclude never concluded anything. The detached-timer helpers are the cure and were already in this module: F5 added them for the settle watchers for this exact reason, and StzReaxisTickDetached passes the argument list through to the callback. The same RunLoop drives them.

methods.name: PendingDataCount
methods.brief: Read by the auto-conclude callback, which is HANDED this object and so must ask it rather than reach into it.

classes.name: stzReactiveSystem
classes.brief: Declarative reactive programming: schedules timers and tasks, makes functions and objects reactive, makes streams and non-blocking HTTP calls, and runs them all in one loop.
classes.description: Create one system, register what should happen (RunAfter, RunEvery, CreateTimer, CreateTask, HttpGet, the stream makers), then call Start: the loop runs the pending tasks, ticks the timers and drains the HTTP answers until nothing is left, the patience runs out or a callback calls Stop. The system sits on a stzReactor when the engine library is present, and falls back to a polling loop when it is not. Callbacks always run on the Ring thread. Timers are named by the id that RunAfter and RunEvery answer; StopTimer and StopAllTimers end them. Reactivate wraps a function or an object so that calls take success and error handlers. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: StopSafe and its five aliases raise the STOPPED banner from the timer they schedule, and BindObjects binds copies, so neither object you pass changes.

methods.name: Status
methods.brief: WHAT HAPPENED, AFTER THE FACT
methods.detail: The class recorded a status, a result and (now) an error, and offered no way to read any of them. A caller whose task failed could not ask what went wrong; a caller whose task succeeded could not collect the answer unless they had registered a handler first.

methods.name: Error
methods.brief: "" when the task has not failed.

methods.name: HasFailed
methods.brief: TRUE if the object has failed.

methods.name: WasReported
methods.brief: Did the failure reach anyone -- a raise, a handler, or stdout? Only ERROR_IGNORE answers FALSE, and it is the one mode that asked to.
methods.detail: Without this the fallback arm had no observable effect at all: removing it left every assertion green, because recording a reason is not reporting it.

methods.name: Complete
methods.brief: AN OUTCOME PRODUCED OUTSIDE Execute()
methods.detail: Not every task computes. stzReactiveObject.SetAsync already HAS the value it is going to store, and its attempt to wrap one in a task function -- `func { return _newValue_ }` -- raised R24, because a Ring lambda cannot read a caller's local. These two let a caller that did the work itself still report it through the same task surface, so Status()/Result()/ Error() mean the same thing however the work happened.

classes.name: stzReactor
classes.brief: Runs timers, TCP and HTTP clients, child programs and servers on a libuv event loop that lives on a thread of its own, and hands the results to Ring by polling.
classes.description: Ring stays synchronous: you submit work and get a job id back at once, then Poll, Await or JobState that id, and no callback ever crosses into Ring. The calls come in families: Submit, Await, Poll and a LastStatus reader for timers, TCP, spawned programs and HTTP, plus one-call forms (TcpRequest, Spawn, HttpGet, HttpPost). A listener (Listen, ListenHttp, ListenStzm and the TLS forms) queues events that ServerPoll or ServerAwait drain as [ :accept, nConn, "" ], [ :data, nConn, cBytes ] or [ :closed, nConn, "" ]; ServerWrite and ServerCloseConn answer on a connection, and the Connect calls dial out and give a channel that is used the same way. A job id is spent once it is drained. The last-status readers (TcpLastStatus, SpawnLastStatus, HttpLastStatus, TlsClientStatus) hold one value for the whole process. The loop starts at the first call and Destroy stops it. Known gap today: Spawn and SubmitSpawn raise error R21 when given a plain text instead of a list.

methods.detail: Each point's refinement is the action "refine-<point>"; To() calls MayProceed(actor, action) so a refinement needs permission (CAN) + authority (SHOULD) covering the point's declared risk tier before it can mutate the source. the NAME of the object that governs this code ("" if none)

methods.name: As

methods.detail: Trust rank (high -> low): :trusted (3, in-process/verified) > :external (2, an external tool) > :sandboxed (1, isolated run) > :llm (0, LLM-composed). A proposal defaults to :trusted; As(posture) declares otherwise for the next To(). The posture rides into the audit chain; a point's TrustFloor refuses anything below the required rank (LLM-composed edits to a critical knob can be forbidden without forbidding a human's).

classes.name: stzRegex
classes.brief: Holds a regular expression compiled by the PCRE2 engine and answers whether, where and how a text matches it, including partial and recursive matches.
classes.description: Build it with a pattern, then call a match method with a text: the text and the outcome of the last call are kept in the object, and the readers (Matches, FindMatches, CaptureGroups, NamedGroups, CaptureByName, the partial and recursive readers) work on that last call. Match asks whether the pattern covers the whole text; MatchFirst and MatchAt search inside it. MatchAsYouType and the partial family serve form validation while a person is still typing, and MatchRecursive handles nested brackets through (?R). A pattern that does not compile does not raise: IsValid answers FALSE and every match call answers FALSE. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: FindMatches and FindCapture skip a character after each match, PartialMatchLength is one too small, RecursiveDepth counts matches rather than nesting, LastError and PatternErrorOffset are stubs, Explain raises for a pattern the library does not know by name, and MatchWordsIn stacks word boundaries on the pattern each time it is called.

methods.name: SignBody
methods.brief: the body-only form: a WEBHOOK's X-Signature
methods.detail: A participant signs the RAW BODY it POSTs, nothing else: no method, no path, no timestamp, no nonce. That is a different message from the canonical string above and the same job: a keyed MAC, compared in constant time, with a replay cache and a ledger line for every refusal. The HMAC runs in the engine. The signature of a body under a key's secret, as hex. Raises on an unknown key.

methods.name: VerifyBody

methods.detail: Why() explains a refusal, and the ledger hears it.

methods.name: VerifyWebhook
methods.brief: THE WEBHOOK VERIFIER.
methods.detail: A hub renews a webhook's secret on a date, so a receiver may hold the old and the new at once: try every key, and answer WHICH one signed it ("" when none). A refusal is ONE ledger line, not one per key tried: unsigned  no signature at all forged    no key recomputes it replayed  a body already believed, inside the window (pnWindowMs from pnNowMs) Outside the window the same body is a fresh delivery again: the cache is bounded by the window, not by traffic. Why() explains.

classes.name: stzScatterPlot
classes.brief: Draws points given as [ h, v ] pairs on two axes: as text for a terminal, as SVG, or as a PNG picture.
classes.description: The points come as pairs, as two lists named H and V (or X and Y), or as labelled points. ToString draws a circle per point on ticked axes with the letters X and Y at the axis ends, and switches to the Ring renderer when the dashed grid or the point labels are on; ToSVG and ToPNG draw one circle per point and carry the coordinates and nothing else, so the grid, labels, letters, axis switches and point character do not reach pixels. The axis letters read the opposite of the usual way (X on the vertical axis), the text picture writes one x tick label per point so many points make them collide, and the pixel picture draws no x tick labels at all; see the warnings. Gallery: doc/gallery/stzScatterPlot/clusters.png (two clusters of 40 points) and negative.png (points around the origin), each with its script, seen wrong by stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG), 2026-10-05, not a person because the horizontal axis carries no numbers; terminal.txt is the text picture of the clusters, read as text and judged wrong because the x tick labels run together.

methods.name: Resize
methods.brief: Adopt a new viewport size. The ENGINE already does this by itself when a scene is drawn into a differently-sized target (that is what makes a resizable window work at all) -- this keeps the FACE's idea of its size equal to the engine's, exactly as stzWindow.Draw already does for a canvas.
methods.detail: It matters more than a reported number: `Project()` divides by the viewport, and the GUI plane's in-scene raycast reads the same size to turn a screen pixel into a ray. A face that still believed its construction size would send every click to the wrong place in a window the user had resized -- silently, since a wrong click looks like a working program doing something else.

methods.name: Shows
methods.brief: Put a DIFFERENT panel on the same quad.
methods.detail: The reason this exists rather than "just mount a new one": an app that reacts to a click by re-declaring its interface produces a NEW stzPanel, and the old one is what the quad is wearing. Mounting again would hang a second quad; keeping the old one shows a screen the user already dismissed. So the quad stays and its skin changes. A panel of a different SIZE gets a new texture, because a texture's dimensions are fixed at birth. When G5's reactive binding lands, this is the seam it replaces: a bound value would change and the same panel would re-lay-out, with no rebuild and no re-upload of unchanged pixels.

methods.name: LooksThrough

methods.detail: THE CAMERA IS COPIED IN, DELIBERATELY AND VISIBLY. Ring copies an object on assignment, so a scene held as `@oScene` is a SNAPSHOT: the panel kept answering with the old lens after the camera moved, and both negative controls in the guard passed at zero error -- which is the engine-wrapper copy law arriving in a plane that has no engine handle to hide behind. Rather than pretend the reference is live, the camera is DATA and the sync is a verb a game loop calls beside Refresh(): oSP.LooksThrough(oScene)     # the camera moved oSP.Refresh()                # the interface changed One line per frame, in the loop that already redraws. A stale mapping is now a missing call rather than an invisible fork.

methods.name: SetClaim
methods.brief: THE SENTENCE THE RULE ASSERTS, in words a reader can disagree with.
methods.detail: Required, and not decoration: half the defects above are a name that promised something the body did not do, and a name is not a sentence.

methods.name: SetScope
methods.brief: WHICH SUBJECTS THIS RULE GOVERNS -- the half no rule in this library has ever stated separately, and the half every scope defect lived in.

methods.name: SetClaimCheck
methods.brief: WHAT MUST BE TRUE of a subject the scope selected.

methods.name: SetCounter
methods.brief: SUBJECTS IT MUST NOT GOVERN. The negative sibling, at rule level.

methods.name: SetReads
methods.brief: WHAT IT READS AND WHAT IT WRITES, so an ordering defect is a fact about declarations rather than something found by rendering a picture and squinting at it.

methods.name: SetOrder
methods.brief: WHEN IT RUNS, in the pipeline it belongs to. Only meaningful against the other rules' orders; the governor compares, never this class.

methods.name: SetUniversal
methods.brief: A RULE THAT IS UNIVERSAL ON PURPOSE, and says why.
methods.detail: Some claims genuinely have no boundary: equal air applies to every picture there is, and no counter-example exists to witness. Without a way to say so, the governor reports every such rule as vacuous forever -- and a governor that reports work nobody can do is one its readers learn to skim, which costs more than the check earns. The REASON is required and is the whole safeguard. "Universal" asserted without one is indistinguishable from a scope predicate that broke, which is the case this layer exists to catch, so the escape hatch has to cost a sentence somebody can disagree with.

classes.name: stzSecretStore
classes.brief: Holds a project's secrets in one registry, with one governed and audited door through which a value can leave.
classes.description: Secrets are registered once by name, so the whole credential surface is enumerable and every entry is self-redacting. Reveal applies the actor gate (only an effectful, non-sandboxed actor passes; a language-model actor is refused) and records the attempt in the access log and in the security ledger, by the secret's name and never its value. RotateToFresh renews a value the store owns, and refuses a secret that lives in an environment variable, a file or a vault, naming where to rotate it. SaveSealedTo writes the store as one authenticated-encryption blob, and StzSecretStoreFromSealedFile reads it back. The store keeps a copy of what it registers.

classes.name: stzSecurityEvent
classes.brief: Holds one typed security record: what happened, who did it, to which thing, how it ended, why, and when.
classes.description: The kind comes from a closed catalog of dotted names (auth.login.failed, secret.reveal.refused ...), and an unknown kind raises. The setters return the event, so calls chain. An event never carries a secret value: About takes the descriptor of an object, never its value. Both clocks are stamped when the event is built, the wall clock for the forensic when and the monotonic clock for ordering, together with the active trace id. An event is recorded in a stzSecurityLedger, and CanonicalString, ToOcsfJson and AsLine are its three serial forms.
classes.example:
o1.ByActorNamed("bob", "external")
o1.About("user:bob")
o1.Refused("bad password")
? o1.AsLine()
#--> REFUSED auth.login.failed by bob (external) on user:bob -- bad password

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an event of one kind from the closed catalog, stamping both clocks and the active trace id at the moment of detection.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: the event kind, a dotted catalog name such as auth.login.failed, matched without regard to case

notes: the outcome starts as refused; severity and technique start at the catalog values for the kind
warnings: an unknown kind raises an error that lists every known kind: the catalog is closed

methods.name: Kind
methods.brief: Returns the catalog name of the event, in lower case.

methods.name: Severity
methods.brief: Returns the severity of the event: info, warning or error.
notes: it starts at the catalog default of the kind and the As calls override it

methods.name: Technique
methods.brief: Returns the MITRE ATT&CK technique id of the kind, or an empty text where no honest mapping exists.

methods.name: Meaning

methods.name: Actor
methods.brief: Returns the name of the actor that did it.
methods.returns: a text; empty until an actor is given

methods.name: Posture
methods.brief: Returns the actor's posture in lower case, such as trusted, sandboxed or external.
methods.returns: a text; empty until an actor is given

methods.name: ActorKinds
methods.brief: Returns the capability kinds the actor object held, as ByActor read them.
methods.returns: a list of text; [ ] for an actor given by name

methods.name: Action
methods.brief: Returns the act that was attempted, trimmed and in lower case.
methods.returns: a text; empty until Doing sets it

methods.name: Risk
methods.brief: Returns the risk tier of the act that was attempted.
methods.returns: a number, 0 until AtRisk sets one

methods.name: Subject
methods.brief: Returns the descriptor of the thing acted on; the value of a secret is never in it.
methods.returns: a text; empty until About sets it

methods.name: Origin
methods.brief: Returns where the event came from, such as an address, a host or an endpoint.
methods.returns: a text; empty until FromOrigin sets it

methods.name: Outcome
methods.brief: Returns how the attempt ended: granted, refused, failed or observed.
methods.returns: a text, refused for a new event

methods.name: Reason
methods.brief: Returns the gate's own words for a refused, failed or observed event.
methods.returns: a text; empty for a grant

methods.name: AtWall
methods.brief: Returns the wall-clock time of the event, in epoch milliseconds.

methods.name: AtMono
methods.brief: Returns the monotonic-clock stamp of the event, in milliseconds, which keeps its ordering across a clock correction.
methods.returns: a number, which may have a fraction
notes: it orders the events of this process only and is not part of the canonical line

methods.name: TraceId
methods.brief: Returns the id of the trace scope that was active when the event was built.
methods.returns: a text; empty outside a trace scope

methods.name: IsRefusal
methods.brief: TRUE if the outcome is refused or failed; a granted or an observed event is not a refusal.

methods.name: ByActor

parameters.name: poActor

methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain
notes: a text sets only the name, so a posture and kinds set earlier stay as they were; an object without Name records its class name

methods.name: ByActorNamed

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the actor name, as text

parameters.name: pcPosture
parameters.role: the actor's posture, stored in lower case, such as external

methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain

methods.name: About
methods.brief: Sets the subject: a text is taken as already safe, an object contributes its redacted descriptor and never its value.

parameters.name: pSubject
parameters.role: a descriptor text such as user:admin, or an object such as a secret

methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain
notes: an object that has neither a descriptor nor a name records its class name
warnings: the redaction law lives here: given a secret it records the descriptor and never reveals it

methods.name: Doing
methods.brief: Sets the act that was attempted, trimmed and put in lower case.

parameters.name: pcAction
parameters.role: the verb, such as reveal or login

methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AtRisk
methods.brief: Sets the risk tier of the act that was attempted; a value that is not a number is ignored.

parameters.name: pnTier
parameters.role: the risk tier, as a number

methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain

methods.name: FromOrigin
methods.brief: Sets where the event came from.

parameters.name: pcOrigin
parameters.role: an address, a host or an endpoint, as text

methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain

methods.name: OccurredAt
methods.brief: Sets the wall time of an event that did not happen now, such as an imported one or a guard needing exact windows.

parameters.name: pnWallMs
parameters.role: the event time, in epoch milliseconds

methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain
notes: a value that is not a number is ignored; the monotonic stamp is left alone, because it cannot be borrowed

methods.name: Granted
methods.brief: Sets the outcome to granted.
methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain
notes: the reason is left as it was

methods.name: Refused
methods.brief: Sets the outcome to refused, with the gate's own words as the reason.

parameters.name: pcReason
parameters.role: the gate's own words, as text

methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Failed
methods.brief: Sets the outcome to failed: the gate admitted the act and it still did not complete.

parameters.name: pcReason
parameters.role: why it did not complete, as text

methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Observed
methods.brief: Sets the outcome to observed, a fact that carries no verdict, such as a session reaching its expiry.

parameters.name: pcReason
parameters.role: what was seen, as text

methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain
notes: an observed event is not a refusal, so no pivot that counts refusals counts it

methods.name: AsInfo
methods.brief: Sets the severity of the event to info, overriding the catalog default.
methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain
notes: OcsfSeverityId and ToOcsfJson on the event itself do use the override
warnings: the ledger keeps the override, but the OCSF exports of the ledger read the catalog default again

methods.name: AsWarning
methods.brief: Sets the severity of the event to warning, overriding the catalog default.
methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain
notes: OcsfSeverityId and ToOcsfJson on the event itself do use the override
warnings: the ledger keeps the override, but the OCSF exports of the ledger read the catalog default again

methods.name: AsError
methods.brief: Sets the severity of the event to error, overriding the catalog default.
methods.returns: the event itself, so calls chain
notes: OcsfSeverityId and ToOcsfJson on the event itself do use the override
warnings: the ledger keeps the override, but the OCSF exports of the ledger read the catalog default again

methods.name: Record
methods.brief: Returns the event as its native record, every field including the actor's kinds and the monotonic stamp.
methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs: kind, severity, technique, actor, posture, actorKinds, action, risk, subject, origin, outcome, reason, atWall, atMono, traceId

methods.name: CanonicalString
methods.brief: Returns the event as one fixed-order line of twelve fields, the form the ledger hashes into its chain.
notes: a vertical bar inside a field is folded to a slash so the line splits back cleanly; two events with the same facts give the same line; the technique, the actor kinds and the monotonic stamp are not in it

methods.name: OcsfSeverityId
methods.brief: Returns the OCSF severity id: 1 informational, 3 medium for a warning, 4 high for an error.

methods.name: OcsfStatusId
methods.brief: Returns the OCSF status id: 1 for a granted event, 2 for every other outcome.
notes: refused and failed both read 2 as well
warnings: an observed event also reads 2, so a fact with no verdict reaches a SIEM as a failure

methods.name: OcsfClassUid
methods.brief: Returns the OCSF class uid chosen from the kind: 3002 for auth, sso and oauth kinds, 4002 for http kinds, 6003 for the rest.
notes: a best-effort mapping: facts that map no field travel under unmapped

methods.name: OcsfCategoryUid
methods.brief: Returns the OCSF category uid of the event's class: 3, 4 or 6.

methods.name: ToOcsfJson

methods.name: AsLine
methods.brief: Returns the event as one readable line: outcome, kind, actor with posture, subject, origin and reason.
methods.returns: a text, for example REFUSED auth.login.failed by bob (external) on route:/pay -- bad password

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Returns the event told as lines of text: kind and severity, meaning, the readable line, both times and the ATT&CK id.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: An identifier, as text.

methods.name: Holds
methods.brief: edges (the meaning is the label) -------------------------------- an actor directly holds a capability

methods.name: Uses
methods.brief: an actor uses a tool

methods.name: Grants

methods.name: Delegates

classes.name: stzSecurityLedger
classes.brief: Keeps security events as evidence: a bounded, hash-chained ring in the engine that can be made durable, anchored off the machine and sealed.
classes.description: Each entry's digest is the SHA-256 of the previous digest and the entry, computed in the engine and never handed in, so an edit to any entry breaks every digest after it and Verify names the first broken link. The ring forgets: past its capacity the oldest events give way, Count keeps counting and Size is what remains. PersistTo writes every event to an insert-only SQLite file and verifies it from the first entry on restart; an anchor sent off the machine shows a cut tail, which a chain alone cannot; SealTo exports a keyed file. A refused kind writes at most a budgeted number of lines per window, so a stranger cannot flush the evidence. The chain detects retroactive edits only, and protects nothing against an attacker already running code in the process. The pivots (OfActor, OfKind, Refusals, Since ...) return records rebuilt from the stored canonical line.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty ring ledger that keeps the newest pnCapacity events; a missing, non-numeric or sub-1 capacity gives 1024.

parameters.name: pnCapacity
parameters.role: how many events the ring keeps, at least 1

notes: the ring lives in the engine and is created at birth, so every copy of the ledger object reads and writes the same events

methods.name: Handle
methods.brief: Returns the engine handle of the ring, creating the ring again first if Destroy had freed it.
notes: StzOpenSecurityLedger passes this handle to the engine as the process ledger

methods.name: AdoptHandle
methods.brief: Binds this object to a ledger owned elsewhere, such as the process ledger, so both read and write the same events.

parameters.name: pEngineHandle
parameters.role: an engine ledger handle, as Handle gives

methods.returns: the ledger itself, so calls chain
notes: the ring this object made first is destroyed; Destroy later leaves an adopted handle alone, because its owner frees it

methods.name: Capacity
methods.brief: Returns how many events the ring can keep, as the engine reports it, even for an object bound to the process ledger.

methods.name: Record
methods.brief: Appends an event to the ring; the engine chains its digest to the previous one, so the caller never supplies a digest.

parameters.name: poEvent
parameters.role: the stzSecurityEvent to append

methods.returns: the ledger itself, so calls chain
notes: a refused kind is subject to the refusal budget and grants never are; past capacity the oldest event is evicted while Count keeps counting
warnings: raises an error when the ledger is durable and the disk write fails: the event is then in memory only

methods.name: AppendCanonical
methods.brief: Appends a canonical line as it is, with the wall time and severity code given, without building an event first.

parameters.name: pcCanonical
parameters.role: the twelve-field line as CanonicalString gives it

parameters.name: pnWallMs
parameters.role: the event time, in epoch milliseconds

parameters.name: pnSeverityCode
parameters.role: 0 for info, 1 for warning, 2 for error

methods.returns: the ledger itself, so calls chain
notes: the path that rebuilds a working ledger from a verified sealed file
warnings: the chain is recomputed here and does not carry the digests of the file the line came from; a line that is not canonical is accepted and reads back with empty fields

methods.name: PersistTo
methods.brief: Makes the ledger durable: later events are also written, in chain order, to an insert-only SQLite file that is checked first.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the SQLite file to create or to resume

notes: call it before recording; after a restart the ring shows the newest window while Count carries the whole history (durable_ledger_narrated)
warnings: a ledger that already holds events, one that is already durable, an unreadable path and a stored history with an edited or missing row are all refused with :ok 0 and nothing is attached

methods.name: IsDurable
methods.brief: TRUE if PersistTo succeeded, so that every event is also written to a file.

methods.name: VerifyDurable
methods.brief: Checks the whole stored chain from the first entry, where Verify can only speak for the retained window.
notes: an edited or removed row shows; a cut tail does not, which is what Anchor is for
warnings: a ledger that is not durable answers :intact 0 with :brokenAt 0 and that message, so ask IsDurable first

methods.name: Count
methods.brief: Returns how many events were ever recorded, including those the ring has already evicted.

methods.name: Size
methods.brief: Returns how many events the ring still holds.
methods.returns: a number, never above the capacity

methods.name: Anchor
methods.brief: Returns the count and head digest of the ledger at this moment, with a one-line text to send off the machine.
notes: the line reads stzledger-anchor:v1: then the count, a colon and the 64-character digest (threat model R5)
warnings: an anchor kept only on the machine that holds the file proves nothing; an empty ledger gives count 0 and 64 zeros, which VerifyAgainstAnchor rejects as malformed in the list form

methods.name: VerifyAgainstAnchor
methods.brief: Checks the durable history against an anchor taken earlier: does the stored file still reach that count with that digest.

parameters.name: pAnchor
parameters.role: the list Anchor returned, or its :line text

notes: :state is holds, truncated, diverged, broken, not-durable, unreadable or malformed; truncated means the tail was cut and diverged means the history was rewritten (ledger_anchor_narrated); only a durable ledger can be checked

methods.name: SetRefusalBudget
methods.brief: Sets how many lines per time window each refused kind may write; past it the engine counts the refusals, writes one marker, then a summary.

parameters.name: pnMax
parameters.role: the lines each refused kind may write per window, 0 turns the budget off

parameters.name: pnWindowMs
parameters.role: the window length, in milliseconds

methods.returns: the ledger itself, so calls chain
notes: the default is 64 per 60000 ms; grants are never budgeted; the budget is counted per kind, so a flood of one kind cannot evict other evidence (ledger_flood_narrated)
warnings: a negative pnMax acts as 0 and turns the budget off, a negative window becomes 1 ms, and neither raises an error

methods.name: RefusalBudget
methods.brief: Returns the refusal budget now in force.
warnings: 64 and 60000 by default

methods.name: Suppressed
methods.brief: Returns how many refusals were counted instead of written, since the ledger was made.
warnings: a flush does not reset it

methods.name: FlushRefusalCounts
methods.brief: Closes every open budget window now and writes each count of suppressed refusals into the chain as one summary line.
methods.returns: the ledger itself, so calls chain
notes: the summary has the outcome observed and the actor ledger, and reads N further refusal(s) of this kind were counted; without a flush a window closes only when the next refusal of that kind arrives after it

methods.name: At
methods.brief: Returns the retained record at a 1-based position, oldest retained first, with its chain digest.

parameters.name: pnIndex
parameters.role: the position among the retained events, 1 is the oldest

methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs, or [ ] when the position is out of range
notes: the keys are kind, severity, actor, posture, action, risk, subject, origin, outcome, reason, atWall, traceId and digest; atMono, technique and actorKinds are not stored

methods.name: All
methods.brief: Returns every retained record, oldest first, each in the shape At gives.
methods.returns: a list of records; [ ] when the ledger is empty
notes: every call rebuilds the records from the stored lines, so on a large ledger keep the result instead of calling it in a loop

methods.name: Recent
methods.brief: Returns the newest records, the oldest of them first.

parameters.name: pnHowMany
parameters.role: how many records to take from the end

methods.returns: a list of records; all of them when pnHowMany exceeds the size, [ ] for 0 or less

methods.name: OfActor
methods.brief: Returns the retained records made by one actor.

parameters.name: pcActor
parameters.role: the actor name

notes: the match is exact and case-sensitive: ALICE does not find alice

methods.name: OfSubject
methods.brief: Returns the retained records about one subject descriptor.

parameters.name: pcSubject
parameters.role: the subject text the event stored, such as user:bob

methods.name: OfKind
methods.brief: Returns the retained records of one event kind.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: the event kind, a dotted catalog name

methods.name: OfTrace
methods.brief: Returns the retained records stamped with one trace id, which ties events to the log lines and spans of one request.

parameters.name: pcTraceId
parameters.role: the trace id, as text

notes: events recorded outside a trace scope carry an empty trace id, which this pivot finds when given an empty text

methods.name: OfOutcome
methods.brief: Returns the retained records that ended one way.

parameters.name: pcOutcome
parameters.role: granted, refused, failed or observed

notes: the match is exact and case-sensitive

methods.name: OfSeverity
methods.brief: Returns the retained records of one severity.

parameters.name: pcSeverity
parameters.role: info, warning or error

notes: the severity is the one stored with the event, which may be an override of the catalog default

methods.name: OfOrigin
methods.brief: Returns the retained records that came from one origin.

parameters.name: pcOrigin
parameters.role: the address, host or endpoint the event stored

notes: an empty text finds the events that carry no origin

methods.name: Refusals
methods.brief: Returns the retained records whose outcome is refused or failed, the signal to watch.
notes: granted and observed records are left out, so an expired session is never counted as a refusal

methods.name: Since
methods.brief: Returns the retained records at or after a wall time.

parameters.name: pnWallMs
parameters.role: the earliest event time, in epoch milliseconds, included

methods.name: Between
methods.brief: Returns the retained records inside a time range, both ends included.

parameters.name: pnFromMs
parameters.role: the start of the range, in epoch milliseconds

parameters.name: pnToMs
parameters.role: the end of the range, in epoch milliseconds

methods.returns: a list of records; [ ] when the start is after the end

methods.name: Digest
methods.brief: Returns the head digest, 64 hex characters, that commits to every event ever recorded, evicted ones included.
notes: an empty ledger answers 64 zeros

methods.name: DigestAt
methods.brief: Returns the chain digest stored with the retained entry at a position.

parameters.name: pnIndex
parameters.role: the position among the retained events, 1 is the oldest

methods.returns: a text; empty when the position is out of range

methods.name: Verify

classes.name: stzSecurityPosture
classes.brief: Runs the security invariants over a project's surface, its secret store, its sites, its actors and its services, and reports findings.
classes.description: It turns the principle that expression is free and admission is governed into a check. The invariants are no-sandboxed-effectful (an error: a sandboxed actor that holds the effectful capability), inline-key, no-central-store and refused-accesses (warnings), and the findings of an attached service registry. Findings are [ :invariant, :severity, :where, :message ] with the severity written error or warn. IsSound means no error; IsClean means nothing flagged at all. The posture keeps a copy of everything handed to it, so describe the surface completely first and ask last.

methods.detail: ASKED IN THE PRODUCTION FRAME, whatever the current phase. "May I go LIVE?" IS the production question, so answering it from a :development phase would have said YES with a fake still bound -- the phase-dependent invariants (sandbox-in-production, ephemeral-in-production) simply had not fired yet. The phase is set, the surface judged, the phase restored: asking is not declaring. methods.detail: The application is a node; every declared service is a node with its posture, its secret name and the phase as properties; an application `depends-on` each of its services. methods.name: Loudness
methods.brief: Integrated loudness in LUFS (ITU-R BS.1770-4), or -1000 for silence.
methods.detail: The standard's K-weighting coefficients are specified at 48 kHz, and the engine REFUSES any other rate rather than applying them anyway. So the face resamples a COPY when it has to -- the caller's sound is not touched, and nobody gets a plausible-looking wrong number.

methods.name: MomentaryLoudness
methods.brief: SS2 -- THE LOUDNESS AN EARCON CAN BE MEASURED WITH.
methods.detail: Loudness() above is INTEGRATED loudness and refuses anything shorter than one 400 ms block, which is every earcon there will ever be. Measured, at peak 0.50: 40, 60, 100 and 200 ms all report -1000 -- this plane's answer for silence -- while 400 ms reports -9.38. A plainly audible sound at half full scale reading as silence is a gap, not a subtlety, and it is why the semantic layer's audibility gate had to start on an unweighted substitute. MomentaryLoudness is the standard's own 400 ms window, ungated, taking the LOUDEST such window rather than a mean -- averaging an earcon against the silence around it answers nothing. BS.1770 arithmetic used as specified, so it is LUFS without qualification.

methods.name: LoudnessOfSupport
methods.brief: The same K-weighting and the same formula over the sound's OWN length.
methods.detail: NOT a standard LUFS figure, and LoudnessMetric() says so -- because the alternative is answering the standard's question wrongly instead of answering a different question honestly. A 60 ms earcon at peak 0.5 reads -9.26 here against -9.27 for the same tone at 400 ms: the two agree to a hundredth of a decibel where the standard has an opinion, which is what makes this trustworthy where it does not.

methods.name: ToCanvas
methods.brief: THE GRAPHICS CONVERGENCE
methods.detail: The sound plane hands a grid of numbers to the graphics plane, which knows how to draw. Neither knows anything about the other's internals: this method speaks only stzCanvas verbs, and stzCanvas has never heard of audio. ONE RECTANGLE PER CELL, because that is what stzCanvas offers -- it has AddRect, AddCircle, AddLine, AddText and no image primitive at all. A full spectrogram would be tens of thousands of rectangles, so the grid is DOWNSAMPLED to the pixel size asked for: each output cell takes the LOUDEST value beneath it, which is the right summary for a spectrogram (a peak that survives is a peak that was there; an average would hide a brief bright partial). Recorded as an SN5 finding: an AddImage on stzCanvas would turn this from thousands of rectangles into one call, and the graphics plane is where that belongs.

methods.name: CaptureInsteadOfDevice
methods.brief: Drain the ring here instead of on a sound card, for `pnSeconds` at most, and keep what came out. Paced: drain at the wall clock's rate; unpaced: as fast as WaitCycles asks.
methods.detail: WHAT IT CANNOT STAND IN FOR: a device drains on ITS OWN thread, so while this thread is busy rendering a new loop's notes the card keeps playing what was posted. classes.name: stzSoundPlot
classes.brief: Draws a sound's analysis, a spectrogram, spectra or a waveform, as a readable picture on a dark plate, in SVG or PNG.
classes.description: Create the plate with a width and a height, set the title and the note, call one Draw method with the analysis it needs, add markers, then ToSVG, SaveAsSVG or SaveAsPNG. The title and the note are read when the Draw method runs, so they must be set before it. The spectrogram uses the inferno colour ramp, the spectra a fixed order of hues with a legend, and every magnitude axis is in decibels. Reach for it when a number about a sound is not enough: it needs the sound engine for the analysis grids, and the PNG needs the graphics device while the SVG does not. Only the first two lines of the note are drawn, and DrawSpectra raises for a starting frequency of 0; see the warnings. Gallery: doc/gallery/stzSoundPlot/spectrogram.png (a sweep), spectra.png (two tones with a marker) and wave.png (beats, with a marker), each with its script, seen right by stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG), 2026-10-05, not a person; wave.png carries thin dark hairlines inside the filled band.
classes.example:
o1.SetNote("A short note.")
? @@( o1.ToNoteLines() )
#--> [ "A short note." ]

methods.brief: MU7: RENDER -- a series of numbers becomes a MELODY in this universe
methods.detail: The plan's MU7 row "data -> melody in a declared universe": sonification that a listener from the tradition would hear as music, not as a meter. The lowest value sits on degree 1 and the highest two octaves of the mode up; one note per beat of the cycle, the cycle's own rhythm under it, the mode's movement and ornaments applied as for any phrase. methods.name: ToneSyllables
methods.brief: MU7 (Niger's row): TEXT -> DRUM
methods.detail: Hausa is tonal: High, Low, and Falling (High then Low on one heavy syllable) -- Newman (1996). In writing the tones are marked the way Newman's dictionary marks them: NO mark is High, a grave (a-grave) is Low, a circumflex (a-circumflex) is Falling; a doubled vowel or a macron is long. Everyday Hausa writing marks NO tones at all -- so text without a single mark is REFUSED: read as all-High it would be a confident lie. ToneSyllables returns what was read; DrumTonesQ plays it on the drum. SayOnDrum is the verb the plan names, and it is GATED: text -> drum is speech only if a Hausa speaker hears the sentence back, and until one has (the declaration's :talkingdrum verdict), it refuses with that reason.

classes.name: stzSplitter
classes.brief: Holds a number of positions, 1 to N, and answers where a string or a list would be cut, as sections [ first, last ] and never as parts.
classes.description: A splitter knows only a size. It never sees the items: every Split method returns a list of sections that a stzString or a stzList then hands to its own Sections method to get the parts. The family has three axes. The cut can fall AT a position or section (the cut-out positions are left out), BEFORE it (the position starts a new section) or AFTER it (the position ends a section); each exists for one position, for several positions, for one section and for several sections, plus SplitToNParts and SplitToPartsOfNItems for even cuts. The IB forms (inclusive bounds, such as SplitAtSectionIB) grow the sections by one part width so the cut positions are kept. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: SplitAround with a flat pair raises R19, SplitAroundSection raises R14, SplitAroundPosition raises R21 for the last position, SplitAtSections reads its first and last cuts before sorting, and the named forms of SplitAt (:ToNParts, :ToPartsOfNItems) raise R14.

methods.name: ToNarration
methods.brief: the document --------------------------------------------------------- EMITTED IN THE SIBLING'S FORMAT, AND PROVISIONAL UNTIL IT SAYS SO. Softanza Narrations owns `.narration`; this writes the v0 grammar it published on 2026-08-11 -- NARRATION, PROSE and CELL, three kinds and no fourth -- and pins that version here so a change there is a change this must be told about rather than one it silently diverges from.
methods.detail: THE ONE LAW OF THAT FORMAT IS HONOURED BY CONSTRUCTION: the document is plain text and outputs are never stored in it. So a caption goes out as PROSE with its holes STILL OPEN, and every number is a CELL that recomputes on arrival. What is written here can be read a year from now and will either recompute to the same numbers or say why not -- which is the whole reason that law exists. The question of whether this shape conforms was routed to the sibling through Central as DN9-EMITTER-01 and is unanswered; silence is not a veto here, so this is written, pinned and marked, and a correction costs one function.

classes.name: stzString
classes.brief: Holds a text and finds, cuts, edits, splits and compares it, character by character, in Unicode.
classes.description: A stzString counts characters, not bytes: positions, lengths and sections are in Unicode codepoints, so Hebrew, Arabic, Chinese and emoji behave like Latin letters. Active forms change the text in place (Remove, Uppercase), passive forms return a changed copy (Uppercased), and the Q forms return the object so calls chain. Reach for it before writing a loop over a text.

classes.name: stzStringChar
classes.brief: Holds one Unicode char and answers questions about it: its codepoint, name, script, case, bidi class and category.
classes.description: Reach for it when a single char deserves more than a one-char stzString. It wraps a stzString and answers from the engine's Unicode data. It is built from a one-char text, a codepoint number, a hex form such as U+0061 or a Unicode char name. A method not defined here falls through to stzString, so a char also answers text questions.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the char object from a one-char text, a codepoint number, a hex form such as U+0061 or 0x61, or a Unicode char name.

parameters.name: pChar
parameters.role: the char: one-char text, codepoint number, U+XXXX or 0xXX hex text, Unicode char name, or a stzString object

notes: an empty text, a text of several chars that is neither a hex form nor a name, and a bare hex such as 61 all raise "Can not create char object!"

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the char held, as a one-char string.

methods.name: String
methods.brief: Returns the held char wrapped in a stzString object, not as plain text.

methods.name: Unicode
methods.brief: Returns the Unicode codepoint of the char, such as 97 for a.

methods.name: UnicodeAsString
methods.brief: Returns the codepoint of the char written as decimal text, such as "97".

methods.name: HexUnicode
methods.brief: Returns the codepoint as U+ followed by four hex digits, such as U+0061.
warnings: known defect: only four hex digits are kept, so a char above U+FFFF comes out wrong: U+1F600 reads U+F600

methods.name: IsEmpty
methods.brief: Answers FALSE every time, because a char object cannot be built empty.

methods.name: Copy
methods.brief: Returns a new stzStringChar object holding the same char, so changing the copy leaves the original alone.

methods.name: IsAString
methods.brief: Answers TRUE every time: a char object counts as a string.

methods.name: Number
methods.brief: Returns the number a digit char stands for, such as 7 for 7, 3 for the Arabic-Indic three, 1 for a circled one.
methods.returns: a number; an empty string for a char with no decimal value
notes: a letter, a Roman numeral and a symbol all answer an empty string

methods.name: Update
methods.brief: Replaces the held char with the given text, in place; a codepoint number empties the object today.

parameters.name: pChar
parameters.role: the new char, as text

notes: written Update("z") or Update(:With = "z")
warnings: known defect: Update(98) leaves an empty string and Unicode 0, because the number is never converted; Update("ab") stores both chars, so only a one-char text works as meant

methods.name: UpdateWith
methods.brief: Replaces the held char with the given one, in place, exactly as the plain form does.

parameters.name: pChar
parameters.role: the new char, as text

warnings: known defect: shares the defect of the plain form, so a codepoint number empties the object

extensions.name: UpdateWithQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Updated
methods.brief: Returns the argument as it came, without converting it or checking it is a char; the object is unchanged.

parameters.name: pChar
parameters.role: the value to hand back

methods.name: CanRetrieveName
methods.brief: Answers TRUE when the Unicode database holds a name for the char, and raises when it does not.
warnings: known defect: for an unnamed code such as U+0378 it raises "Can't proceed!" instead of answering FALSE, because it asks for the name and the name request raises

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the official Unicode name, such as LATIN SMALL LETTER A, and raises when the database has none.
notes: a control char answers <control>; the first char of a range answers a range label such as <Private Use, First>; an unassigned code such as U+0378 raises

methods.name: NameIs
methods.brief: TRUE if the char carries the given Unicode name; the comparison ignores case.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: A name, as text.

notes: NameIs("latin small letter a") is TRUE for a

methods.name: AsciiCode
methods.brief: Returns the ASCII code of the char, 0 to 127; for a char above 127 it raises R3 instead of a clear message.
warnings: known defect: the failure branch calls stzCharError, which is defined nowhere, so a non-ASCII char raises R3 "Calling Function without definition"

methods.name: Orientation
methods.brief: Returns "ltr" or "rtl", the writing direction of the char as the string layer judges it.
notes: judged by script block: a char of the Arabic range, even the shaddah or U+FEFF, answers rtl where UnicodeDirection says nonspacingmark or boundaryneutral

methods.name: UnicodeDirection
methods.brief: Returns the name of the char's Unicode bidi class, such as lefttoright, europeannumber or whitespace.
notes: other names seen: righttoleft, righttoleftarabic, arabicnumber, otherneutrals, nonspacingmark

methods.name: UnicodeDirectionNumber
methods.brief: Returns the bidi class as a number written as text, in Qt numbering: 0 left-to-right, 1 right-to-left, 2 European number, 9 whitespace.
notes: the other values: 3 separator, 4 terminator, 5 Arabic number, 6 common separator, 7 paragraph, 8 section, 10 neutral, 13 Arabic letter, 17 nonspacing mark, 18 boundary neutral

methods.name: IsVowel
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is one of the ASCII vowels a, e, i, o, u in either case; an accented vowel answers FALSE.

methods.name: IsLeftToRight
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is left-to-right, or a left-to-right embedding, override or isolate mark.
notes: a digit answers FALSE: its class is European number

methods.name: IsRightToLeft
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is right-to-left, as for Hebrew and Arabic letters, or the char is an RLE, RLO or RLI mark.

methods.name: IsArabicFraction
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is in the library's list of fraction chars, such as the vulgar half U+00BD or U+2153.

methods.name: IsEuropeanNumberSeparator
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is European number separator, as for the plus sign and the hyphen-minus.

methods.name: IsEuropeanNumberTerminator
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is European number terminator, as for the dollar and percent signs.

methods.name: IsIndianDigit
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is one of the library's Indian digits: the Arabic-Indic digits U+0660 to 0669 and most Persian ones.
notes: Devanagari digits answer FALSE, and so do the Persian U+06F4 to 06F7

methods.name: IsCommonNumberSeparator
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is common number separator, as for the comma, the full stop and the fraction slash.

methods.name: IsParagraphSeparator
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is paragraph separator, as for the newline and U+2029.

methods.name: IsSectionSeparator
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is segment separator, which is the tab char.

methods.name: IsWhitespace
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is whitespace, as for the plain space and U+2028; a tab, a newline and a no-break space answer FALSE.

methods.name: IsOrientationNeutral
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is other neutral, as for parentheses, or if the char is a digit.
notes: the digit clause makes 7 answer TRUE although its class is European number

methods.name: IsLeftToRightEmbedding
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is the left-to-right embedding mark, U+202A.

methods.name: IsLeftToRightOverride
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is the left-to-right override mark, U+202D.

methods.name: IsLeftToRightIsolate
methods.brief: Returns an empty string today instead of TRUE for the left-to-right isolate mark, U+2066.
warnings: known defect: the body is only a comment ("Reserved for future implementation"), so the answer is always empty

methods.name: IsRightToLeftIsolate
methods.brief: Returns an empty string today instead of TRUE for the right-to-left isolate mark, U+2067.
warnings: known defect: the body is only a comment ("Reserved for future implementation"), so the answer is always empty

methods.name: IsRightToLeftArabic
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is right-to-left Arabic, as for Arabic letters and Arabic presentation forms.

methods.name: IsRightToLeftEmbedding
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is the right-to-left embedding mark, U+202B.

methods.name: IsRightToLeftOverride
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is the right-to-left override mark, U+202E.

methods.name: IsPopDirectionalFormat
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is the pop directional formatting mark, U+202C, which ends an embedding or override.

methods.name: IsNonSpacingMark
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is nonspacing mark, as for combining accents and the Arabic shaddah.

methods.name: IsBoundaryNeutral
methods.brief: TRUE if the bidi class is boundary neutral, as for control chars, the soft hyphen and U+FEFF.

methods.name: UnicodeCategoryNumber
methods.brief: Returns the Unicode general-category code of the char, from the engine: 1 Lu, 2 Ll, 5 Lo, 9 Nd, 18 Po, 23 Zs, 26 Cc.

methods.name: UnicodeCategory
methods.brief: Returns the name of the Unicode general category, such as letter_lowercase, number_decimaldigit or punctuation_dash.

methods.name: IsArabicShaddah
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is U+0651, the Arabic shaddah.

methods.name: IsLetter
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine counts the char as a letter, or if it is the Arabic shaddah, which the library treats as a letter.

methods.name: IsNotLetter
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is not a letter, so for digits, spaces, punctuation and accents; the shaddah answers FALSE.

methods.name: IsLetterOrSpaceOrChar
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a letter, a Unicode space, or equal to the given char.

parameters.name: c
parameters.role: the extra char that also qualifies

methods.name: IsTheLetter
methods.brief: TRUE if the char equals the given char once both are uppercased, so the test ignores case.

parameters.name: c
parameters.role: the char to compare with

notes: any char works, not only letters

methods.name: IsLetterOrNumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a letter or a digit char, in any script, or a circled digit.
notes: a Roman numeral answers FALSE

methods.name: IsLetterOrSpace
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a letter or a Unicode space, a newline included.

methods.name: IsLetterOrSpaceOrThisChar
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a letter, a Unicode space, or equal to the given char.

parameters.name: pcChar
parameters.role: A single character.

methods.name: IsEuropean
methods.brief: Raises error R14 today instead of TRUE for a European number, separator or terminator.
warnings: known defect: the body calls IsEuropeanNumber, which is defined nowhere

methods.name: IsSpace
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine counts the char as a space: the plain space, a tab, a newline or the no-break space.
notes: U+2028 and U+2029 answer FALSE

methods.name: IsUnicodeNumber
methods.brief: Answers TRUE for Arabic, Hebrew or CJK letters and FALSE for 7 today, instead of TRUE for number chars.
warnings: known defect: it tests category codes 3, 4 and 5, which are title-case, modifier and other letters in the engine's numbering, where digits are 9 to 11; Roman, Mandarin and Indian numerals are caught by their own tests

methods.name: IsNotNumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is neither a decimal digit nor a circled digit.
notes: a Roman numeral answers TRUE

methods.name: IsDigit
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine counts the char as a decimal digit, in any script: 7, the Arabic-Indic three, the Devanagari one.
notes: a circled digit answers FALSE

methods.name: IsArabicNumber
methods.brief: Answers FALSE for 0 to 9 and raises R41 for a non-ASCII digit today, instead of TRUE for an Arabic digit.
warnings: known defect: it searches a list of digit texts for a number, so a plain digit is never found, and it adds 0 to the content, which raises R41 "Invalid numeric string" for an Arabic-Indic, Devanagari or circled digit

methods.name: IsANumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a decimal digit in any script or a circled digit.

methods.name: IsIndianNumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is in the library's list of Indian digits, the Arabic-Indic and most Persian digits.

methods.name: IsRomanNumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a Roman numeral char, such as U+2160 or U+2171, from the library's list.

methods.name: IsMandarinNumber
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a Mandarin numeral from the library's list: 〇, 一 to 十, 百, 千 or 万.

methods.name: IsAscii
methods.brief: TRUE if the codepoint is below 128, control chars included.

methods.name: IsAsciiLetter
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is an unaccented ASCII letter, A to Z or a to z.

methods.name: IsPunctuation
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine counts the char as punctuation, such as ( ) - or !.
notes: the dollar sign and the infinity sign are symbols and answer FALSE

methods.name: IsGeneralPunctuation
methods.brief: TRUE if the char lies in the Unicode General Punctuation block, U+2000 to U+206F.
notes: the comma and the exclamation mark are not in this block

methods.name: IsSupplementalPunctuation
methods.brief: TRUE if the char lies in the library's Supplemental Punctuation range, U+2DF6 to U+2E7F.

methods.name: IsSymbol
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine counts the char as a symbol, such as $, the infinity sign or an emoji.

methods.name: IsNonChar
methods.brief: TRUE if the codepoint is a Unicode noncharacter: U+FDD0 to U+FDEF, or a codepoint ending in FFFE or FFFF.

methods.name: IsMark
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine counts the char as a combining mark, such as an accent or the Arabic shaddah.

methods.name: IsSeparator
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine counts the char as a space: the plain space, a tab, a newline or the no-break space.

methods.name: IsOneOfThese
methods.brief: TRUE if the char appears in the given list of chars.

parameters.name: pacChars
parameters.role: the list of chars to look in

methods.name: IsWordSeparator
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is in the library's word separators: space . , ; : ! ? the Arabic comma and question mark, the apostrophes and the em dash.

methods.name: IsSentenceSeparator
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is in the library's sentence separators: the full stop, ! , ? and the Arabic question mark.

methods.name: IsLineSeparator
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is the newline, char 10, and nothing else; U+2028 answers FALSE.

methods.name: IsWordNonLetterChar
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is in the library's non-letter word chars: _ - * / \ + and the digits 0 to 9.

methods.name: IsMirrored
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a bracket pair member the library can mirror, such as ( ) < > [ ] { } or the guillemets.

methods.name: UnicodeOfMirrored
methods.brief: Returns the codepoint of the char's mirror partner, 41 for ( and 62 for <, or the char's own codepoint if it has none.

methods.name: Mirrored
methods.brief: Raises error R3 today instead of returning the mirror partner of the char.
warnings: known defect: the body calls CharFromUnicode, which is defined nowhere

methods.name: IsLatin
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine's Unicode data puts the char in the Latin script, an accented letter included.

methods.name: IsLatinLetter
methods.brief: TRUE if the char is a letter of the Latin script, accented letters included.

methods.name: IsBasicLatin
methods.brief: Raises error R24 today instead of testing for the Basic Latin block, U+0000 to U+007F.
warnings: known defect: the body reads _anBasicLatinUnicodes, but the data file defines _anLatinBasicUnicodes

methods.name: IsLatin1Supplement

methods.name: XorEncrypt
methods.brief: XOR with a repeating passphrase, returned as BASE64.
methods.detail: Two bugs lived here. The key was passed as a string HANDLE to an engine function whose key parameter is a single BYTE, so the bridge coerced the pointer to a number and every call XORed with a different arbitrary byte -- "Secret" encrypted and decrypted with "key" came back "Pf`qfw", every byte off by a constant 0x03, the gap between the two accidental keys. And the result is BINARY. Every other cipher here permutes letters and stays in the text domain; XOR does not. The engine's string type validates UTF-8 (rightly), so feeding raw cipher bytes back in for decryption dropped them: "Secret"/"key" happens to produce only ASCII-range bytes and survived, but two Arabic letters produce B5 D0 A1 E0, which is not valid UTF-8, and came back empty. So the cipher now stays inside the engine and what crosses the bridge is always base64. XorDecrypt is a real method rather than an alias for XorEncrypt: the pair is still an involution over the BYTES, but the encoding step has a direction.

methods.name: HtmlEncoded
methods.brief: The string with the HTML-special chars encoded as entities.
methods.detail: Engine-backed. This built a per-character LIST of the whole string and concatenated onto a growing result -- the wrap-to-scan shape, quadratic in the string length. The engine does the same five substitutions (& < > " and ' -> ') in one pass, and the bridge now sizes its buffer to fit rather than silently returning "" past 64 KB.

methods.name: HtmlDecoded
methods.brief: The string with the HTML entities decoded. Engine-backed, and it HAS to be, because the old Ring version was wrong.
methods.detail: It ran StzReplace("&", "&") FIRST, then the others -- so the '&' produced by decoding & was fed straight into the next rules: "&lt;"  ->  "<"  ->  "<"      WRONG, should stay "<" "&gt;"  ->  ">"  ->  ">"      WRONG, should stay ">" i.e. anything that was DOUBLE-encoded came back single-decoded. The encode/decode pair was not a round trip whenever the source text itself contained an entity. The engine makes ONE left-to-right pass, consuming each entity whole and advancing past it, so a decoded '&' can never re-trigger a match. It also covers '   and numeric entities (&#NN; / &#xHH;), which the five-replace version silently left intact -- a widening, not a behaviour change for anything the old code handled.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Accepts a string, an stzString, OR a bare engine handle (a number).
methods.detail: THE HANDLE FORM EXISTS BECAUSE THE OBJECT FORM COPIES. Ring duplicates an object when it is assigned to an attribute, so `new stzStringFinder(This)` copied the entire string -- and stzString creates a finder per call in 20 methods, making its class surface SLOWER than the bare global functions (26.70 ms vs 12.36 for 200 finds over 180 KB) despite being the side that holds a resident engine handle. Seventeen of this class's uses of @oString are `.Engine()` -- a number. Passing that number directly costs nothing, and the full stzString is rebuilt LAZILY (from the engine's own bytes) only for the handful of methods that need more: Content, NumberOfChars, IsEmpty, StartsWithCS, EndsWithCS, SubStrings, _FindSubStr.

classes.name: stzStringList
classes.brief: Holds a list of strings and answers questions about it: find, count, sort, filter, replace, split and change case.
classes.description: Reach for it when the strings of a list are the subject and a stzList is more than you need. It checks at birth that every item is a string, and the per-string work goes to the engine. Methods such as Add, SortInAscending, Unique, ToUpper and Trim change the list in place; the Sorted, Uppercased and Trimmed forms return a plain Ring list and leave it alone. Search methods come in a case-sensitive form and a CS form that takes a flag, as in FindCS(pcStr, 0).

methods.name: ScriptCount
methods.brief: How many scripts the string uses -- COMMON INCLUDED.
methods.detail: Common is the bucket for digits, spaces and punctuation. Counting it is the ruled definition, and it makes this agree with stzStringText.Scripts(), which has always LISTED common as a script of its own. The two used to disagree on ordinary text: "hello 123"          Scripts() [latin, common]  = 2, here 1 arabic + " latin"    [arabic, common, latin]    = 3, here 2 "   "                [common]                   = 1, here 0 Two methods answering "how many scripts" with different numbers is the kind of split a caller only discovers by accident, so they now match.

methods.name: ScriptCountExcludingCommon
methods.brief: Scripts EXCLUDING common -- the count of real writing systems.

methods.name: IsMixedScript
methods.brief: Deliberately NOT ScriptCount() > 1.
methods.detail: "Mixed script" means mixing writing systems -- Latin with Cyrillic, the shape of a homograph attack. Digits and spaces are not a second writing system, so counting common here would make "hello 123", and every invoice line ever written, mixed-script.

classes.name: stzSurfacePlot
classes.brief: Draws parts of a whole as a treemap whose cell areas are proportional to the values: as text, SVG or PNG.
classes.description: Despite its name it draws no function surface: it is a composition plot. The data is positive numbers, or label = number pairs, and the largest values get the largest cells. ToString draws box-drawing borders with a name centred in each cell; ToSVG and ToPNG draw coloured rectangles with the name and the share of the total, which :ShowValues = 0 removes. Setters answer the plot itself so calls can be chained, unlike the other plot classes. In the text picture a name wider than its cell is cut at both ends (Support reads upp.), values and percentages together run into each other, and in the pixel picture parts too small for a label get none; see the warnings. Gallery: doc/gallery/stzSurfacePlot/budget.png (five departments), seen right by stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG), 2026-10-05, not a person; manyparts.png (twelve parts, seven with no label), seen uncertain by the same pass; terminal.txt is the text picture, read as text and judged wrong because a label is clipped.

notes: it is not a function surface: it draws shares of a total
warnings: Zero and negative values raise "You must provide only positive numbers", and an empty list is accepted but its picture then raises "the engine could not render this plot"

notes: each cell carries its name and its share of the total unless :ShowValues = 0 removes all text, and without a Font option there is none anyway
warnings: Percent, value, border and label switches set on this object do not carry over to pixels

classes.brief: Holds a table of named columns and numbered rows, and answers questions about its cells, rows and columns.
classes.description: Reach for it when data has columns that deserve a name and rows that deserve a position. The content is stored column by column, as [ name, list of cells ] pairs, so a column is reached by its name (case does not matter) or by its position, and a row only by its position. A table is built from rows whose first line holds the column names, from rows alone (the columns are then called col1, col2 ...), from a hash list of name = cells pairs, or from a [ columns, rows ] size pair. Mutators change the table in place and return nothing; the CQ forms and the Sorted and Filled families give a result without touching it. The class inherits stzList, so a method not defined here falls through to the list. Many names are alternative spellings of one method, and a good share of the class is unfinished: about 200 methods raise an error or do nothing today, and each of them says so in its brief and its warning.
